extractions.source_summary: Card cites ATL-PHYS-PUB-2015-022, "Expected performance of the ATLAS b-tagging algorithms in Run-2" (ATLAS Collaboration, 2015; MV2c20 tagger, simulation-only public note) — appropriate WP context but not peer-reviewed and gives no tabulated pT-binned numbers in extractable form. Best citable peer-reviewed corroboration: ATLAS Collaboration, "ATLAS b-jet identification performance and efficiency measurement with tt-bar events in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV," Eur. Phys. J. C 79 (2019) 970, arXiv:1907.05120. Its Table 4 (MV2 single-cut OPs on baseline tt-bar) gives, at the eps_b=70% OP: c-jet rejection 8.9 (c-mistag ~0.112), light-flavour jet rejection 300 (light-mistag ~0.0033). The b-eff vs pT shape (turn-on, plateau ~0.73 around 75-200 GeV, high-pT falloff) is shown in Fig. 8/9. The Delphes functional forms reproduce the 70% inclusive WP and the rejection magnitudes well across the bulk of the jet pT spectrum. Note the tagger generation differs (card era MV2c20 vs measured MV2/MV2c10), but the 70% WP performance is consistent. Consider also EPJC 79 (2019) 970 Table 4 as the primary citable number for c-/light-mistag.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card formulas have NO eta dependence (functions of pt only). Sources are inclusive over |eta|<2.5 (jet pT>=20 GeV), so there is no per-eta binning to match — card omits the eta dependence that exists in the real detector (b-eff and light-rejection degrade toward |eta|~2.5; see 1907.05120 Fig. 11). pT: card is a smooth continuous function; source Table 4 numbers are inclusive over the tt-bar pT spectrum, while Fig. 8 gives the pT shape. No discrete pT-bin mismatch, but card is a fit/shape choice rather than tabulated bins.

coefficients.name: light_mistag_PDG0_const
coefficients.applicability: light-flavour jets (PDG 0), |eta|<2.5, pT>=20 GeV; ~70% b-eff WP
coefficients.locator: EPJC 79 (2019) 970, Table 4 (MV2, eps_b=70% single-cut OP): light-flavour jet rejection = 300
coefficients.extracted_value: light mistag = 1/300 = 0.0033 (inclusive over tt-bar spectrum). Card formula gives ~0.0021-0.0035 over pT~20-200 GeV (low-pT asymptote 0.002).
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: unknown (Table 4 lists no per-OP uncertainty; rejection has ~10-20% spread across pT, see Fig.2)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Card low-pT light mistag (0.002) and bulk values (~0.0025-0.0035) bracket the source inclusive light mistag 1/300=0.0033; functional form linearly rising in pT is a reasonable approximation of degrading light-rejection at high pT.

coefficients.name: light_mistag_PDG0_slope
coefficients.locator: EPJC 79 (2019) 970, Fig. 2(a) (light-flavour rejection vs eps_b) and Fig.8/pT-dependent rejection; Table 4 inclusive value 300
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated as a slope; light mistag rises with pT (rejection drops at high pT). Card slope yields mistag rising from 0.002 (pT~0) to ~0.0093 at 1 TeV (rejection ~107).
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Slope encodes the known increase of light-jet mistag with pT; magnitude (rejection ~300 in bulk falling toward ~100 at TeV scale) is qualitatively and quantitatively compatible with ATLAS measured trend. No public tabulated slope exists, so cannot tighten further.

coefficients.name: c_mistag_PDG4_amplitude
coefficients.locator: EPJC 79 (2019) 970, Table 4 (MV2, eps_b=70% single-cut OP): c-jet rejection = 8.9
coefficients.extracted_value: c mistag = 1/8.9 = 0.112 (inclusive). Card formula peaks at ~0.144 (pT~75-100 GeV), giving rejection ~7; falls to ~0.07 (rejection ~14) at high pT.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: unknown (Table 4 no per-OP unc.; Fig.2(b) shows ~factor spread vs pT)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (optionally lower peak amplitude ~0.16 to bring peak c-mistag from 0.144 to ~0.112 matching rejection 8.9, if exact-WP match desired)
coefficients.rationale: Card peak c-mistag 0.144 (rejection ~7) vs source inclusive 0.112 (rejection 8.9): same order, card mildly pessimistic on c-rejection at the peak but consistent within the pT spread; shape (turn-on then falloff) matches expected c-tagging behaviour.

coefficients.name: c_mistag_PDG4_turnon
coefficients.locator: EPJC 79 (2019) 970, Fig. 8 (b/c efficiency vs pT) and Table 4 inclusive c-rejection 8.9
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated as coefficients; encodes turn-on by ~50-75 GeV and gentle high-pT decline. Resulting c-mistag plateau ~0.11-0.14 over pT~50-200 GeV consistent with rejection ~7-9.
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Shape parameters produce a c-mistag profile consistent with the measured ~70% WP c-rejection across the bulk pT range; no public tabulation of these exact coefficients, so retain.

coefficients.name: b_eff_PDG5_amplitude
coefficients.locator: EPJC 79 (2019) 970, Table 4 (eps_b=70% OP, selection MV2D>0.83) and Fig. 8 / Fig. 9(b-eff vs pT)
coefficients.extracted_value: Target inclusive b-eff = 0.70; measured b-eff vs pT (Fig.8) turns on from ~0.5 at 20-30 GeV, plateaus ~0.75-0.80 at 100-300 GeV, falls at multi-hundred GeV. Card gives 0.53(20)/0.60(30)/0.67(50)/0.73 plateau(75-200)/0.49(500 GeV).
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: scale-factor/total ~2-5% in bulk, rising to ~10-15% at high pT (Fig.9, Table 5)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Card b-eff turn-on, ~0.73 plateau, and high-pT falloff reproduce the measured 70% single-cut OP pT profile of the MV2 tagger; inclusive average lands near the 70% WP. Card is consistent with EPJC 79 (2019) 970 Fig.8/9 and Table 4 within measurement uncertainties.

extractions.source_summary: Functional form sqrt(a^2 + (b*pt)^2) is the ATLAS inner-detector (ID) track momentum-resolution parametrization sigma_ID(pt)/pt = aID(eta) (+) bID(eta)*pt, Eq.(2) of ATLAS Collaboration, "Measurement of the muon reconstruction performance of the ATLAS detector using 2010 LHC pp collision data at sqrt(s)=7 TeV", arXiv:1404.4562 [hep-ex] (submitted 17 Apr 2014; ID resolution: Sec.10, Eq.(2) on p.18-19, Figs.17-18 on p.20-21). aID = multiple-scattering term, bID = intrinsic (field/spatial-resolution/misalignment) term; aID set to MC (constrained by ID material measurements [11,12] to within 5% barrel / 10% endcap), bID fit from Z->mumu dimuon-mass resolution. NOTE: the journal reference written in the card comment, EPJC 74 (2014) 3130, is actually the SEPARATE 2011/2012 (7-8 TeV) muon paper (arXiv:1407.3935); arXiv:1404.4562 (the 2010/7 TeV paper) is what physically contains Eq.(2) + Figs.17-18. Both papers use the identical Eq.(2) form. CRITICAL CAVEAT: neither paper publishes a liftable (aID,bID) numeric table -- the values live only as curves in Figs.17-18, and they describe MUON ID tracks, not charged hadrons. The card's charged-hadron (a,b) numbers are NOT lifted from this source; they are the generic Delphes ATLAS-card defaults. The paper authoritatively supports only the functional form and the rough scale of the ID resolution.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Severe mismatch. Card eta bins: |eta|<=0.5, 0.5-1.5, 1.5-2.5. Source (Figs.17-18) eta regions: Barrel |eta|<1.05, Transition 1.05-1.7, End-Cap 1.7-2.0, No-TRT 2.0-2.5. Card boundaries 0.5/1.5 have no counterpart in the source; the source's natural boundaries (1.05/1.7/2.0) reflect ATLAS detector geometry. Card bins are a Delphes choice (the same mismatch is flagged in the adjacent MuonMomentumSmearing provenance comment, lines 188-189).

coefficients.name: a_charged_eta0_05 (constant/MS term, |eta|<=0.5)
coefficients.applicability: charged hadrons, |eta|<=0.5, pt>0.1 GeV; constant (low-pt plateau) term of sigma(pt)/pt
coefficients.locator: Eq.(2) (p.18-19) + Fig.17 'Barrel ID (|eta|<1.05)' panel (p.20); aID read as the low-pt plateau of sigma/pt curve
coefficients.extracted_value: aID(barrel) ~ 0.015 (plot-read, smeared-simulation curve low-pt plateau; not tabulated)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~5% relative on aID (text: ID material constrains aID to MC within 5% in barrel)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Flag for review; keep 0.06 only if hadron-specific. Muon-ID measured plateau is ~0.015 (~1.5%), i.e. ~4x smaller than the card's 0.06. If the card intends to track the ID resolution it is strongly pessimistic; rationale: card a=6% vs measured muon-ID ~1.5%. No public source gives a 6% hadron constant term, so cannot set a firm revised number.
coefficients.rationale: Functional form matches Eq.(2), but the numeric constant term (6%) is ~4x the muon-ID value read off Fig.17 Barrel ID (~1.5%); the card number is not lifted from this source and is a Delphes default. Charged-hadron-specific degradation could justify a larger a, but no public source documents 6%.

coefficients.applicability: charged hadrons, |eta|<=0.5, pt>0.1 GeV; pt-multiplicative (intrinsic) term
coefficients.locator: Eq.(2) + Fig.17 'Barrel ID (|eta|<1.05)' panel (p.20); bID inferred from high-pt rise (sigma/pt ~0.08 at pt=200 GeV, smeared curve)
coefficients.extracted_value: bID(barrel) ~ 3.9e-4 GeV^-1 (smeared/data) or ~3e-4 (MC); plot-read from sqrt(0.08^2-0.015^2)/200
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: shaded band ~ +/-10-15% relative on the high-pt curve

coefficients.rationale: Card slope (1.3e-3) is ~3x the muon-ID slope read from Fig.17 Barrel ID (~3.9e-4 smeared). Number not lifted from this source; Delphes default, pessimistic relative to muon ID.

coefficients.applicability: charged hadrons, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5, pt>0.1 GeV; pt-slope term

coefficients.applicability: charged hadrons, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>0.1 GeV; constant term
coefficients.locator: Eq.(2) + Fig.18 'End-Cap ID (1.7<|eta|<2.0)' (aID~0.033) and 'No-TRT ID (2.0<|eta|<2.5)' (aID~0.045) panels (p.21); plot-read low-pt plateau
coefficients.extracted_value: aID(endcap) ~ 0.033; aID(no-TRT) ~ 0.045 (card bin 1.5-2.5 spans both; not tabulated, plot-read)

coefficients.name: b_charged_eta15_25 (intrinsic/slope term, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5)
coefficients.applicability: charged hadrons, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>0.1 GeV; pt-slope term
coefficients.locator: Eq.(2) + Fig.18 'End-Cap ID (1.7<|eta|<2.0)' panel (p.21): sigma/pt ~0.185 at pt=200 GeV; No-TRT panel plotted vs pt/tan^2(theta)

Also note source uses pt/tan^2(theta) (not pt) for |eta|>2.0, which the card's pure-pt form does not capture.

extractions.source_summary: ATLAS Collaboration, "Charged-particle distributions in sqrt(s)=13 TeV pp interactions measured with the ATLAS detector at the LHC," Phys. Lett. B 758 (2016) 67-88, arXiv:1602.01633 (STDM-2015-02). This is the authoritative public, peer-reviewed ATLAS reference for the inner-detector primary charged-particle track reconstruction efficiency vs eta and pT in Run 2 (13 TeV). Figure 2(c) gives efficiency vs eta (integrated over pT>500 MeV, |eta|<2.5); Figure 2(d) gives efficiency vs pT (integrated over |eta|<2.5). Section 6.3 defines the efficiency as N_matched(pT,eta)/N_generated(pT,eta) for primary charged particles. NOTE: this measurement is restricted to pT>500 MeV, whereas the Delphes card's lowest non-zero bin starts at pT=0.1 GeV; there is therefore no public ATLAS measurement of the 0.1-0.5 GeV efficiency from this paper. The current card values (0.70/0.95 central, 0.60/0.85 forward) are the long-standing generic Delphes ATLAS-card defaults and are NOT traceable to a cited measurement (audit_ATLAS.md line 25 marks the source as 'needed').
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card eta breakpoint is at |eta|=1.5 (central) and |eta|=2.5 (acceptance edge). The source (Fig 2c) is binned finely and continuous in eta over |eta|<2.5; it shows the efficiency is NOT flat within |eta|<1.5 (it peaks ~0.87 at eta~0 and falls to ~0.80 by |eta|=1.5) nor within 1.5<|eta|<2.5 (~0.80 falling to ~0.65 at |eta|=2.5 with a local rise to ~0.76 near |eta|=2.2). The card's 2-bin eta step model is a coarse approximation of a smoothly varying curve. pT binning mismatch: card splits at pT=0.1 and 1.0 GeV; source covers only pT>0.5 GeV (Fig 2d), so the card's 0.1-1.0 GeV bin is below the measured range and the >1 GeV plateau in the source is ~0.85-0.88, not 0.95.

coefficients.name: eff_pt_below_0p1_threshold
coefficients.locator: Fig 2(d) lower kinematic limit (measurement starts at pT=500 MeV); Sec 6.3 / Sec 3 (selection pT>500 MeV)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (below measured range; reconstruction efficiency for pT<0.1 GeV is effectively ~0 because such low-pT charged particles do not reach/leave enough hits in the silicon tracker)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: A hard zero below pT=0.1 GeV is a physically reasonable acceptance cutoff (very low-pT tracks curl up in the 2T field and fail reconstruction), but no public ATLAS measurement quantifies efficiency at pT<0.1 GeV; the cited paper only covers pT>0.5 GeV. Keep as a conservative acceptance floor.

coefficients.name: eff_central_lowpt
coefficients.locator: Fig 2(d) (eff vs pT, |eta|<2.5) at pT~0.5-1 GeV; Fig 2(c) central region
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.78-0.80 at pT=0.5-1.0 GeV (plot-read from Fig 2d); central eta-integrated plateau ~0.85 (Fig 2c). Card bin 0.1-1.0 GeV partly below measured range.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~0.7% (central) systematic on the efficiency at fixed point; 3.5% additional non-primary/closure-type effect at pT=500 MeV per Sec 6.3/Table
coefficients.proposed_revision: ~0.78 +/- 0.02 for the 0.5-1.0 GeV part of the bin (Fig 2d at pT~0.5-1 GeV); the 0.1-0.5 GeV part is unmeasured. Rationale: card's 0.70 is ~8% lower than the measured ~0.78 at 0.5-1 GeV, but the card bin extends down to 0.1 GeV where efficiency is unmeasured/lower, so 0.70 is a defensible bin-average. Flag as approximate.
coefficients.rationale: Read from Fig 2(d): efficiency rises from ~0.78 at pT=500 MeV. Card value 0.70 is plausibly the average once the unmeasured 0.1-0.5 GeV (lower-efficiency) region is folded in; cannot fully confirm because that sub-range has no public measurement.

coefficients.name: eff_central_highpt
coefficients.locator: Fig 2(d) (eff vs pT, |eta|<2.5) for pT>1 GeV; Fig 2(c) central eta region |eta|<1.5
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.85-0.88: Fig 2(d) plateaus at ~0.86 (pT~10 GeV) rising to ~0.88 at high pT; Fig 2(c) central (|eta|<1.5) values range ~0.80 (at |eta|=1.5) to ~0.87 (eta~0), eta-integrated ~0.85
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~0.7% syst (central region, Sec 6.3); total efficiency uncertainty 0.5-1.4% (eta), 0.7% (pT) per uncertainty table p.12
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.86 +/- 0.02 (read from Fig 2d plateau and Fig 2c central average). Rationale: card's 0.95 is ~0.09-0.10 (about 10%) HIGHER than the measured ATLAS plateau of ~0.85-0.88; the card is optimistic because the real efficiency is limited by detector material losses (~12-15% inefficiency in the barrel).
coefficients.rationale: Fig 2(c)/(d): the measured central tracking efficiency plateaus near 0.85-0.88, not 0.95. The card overstates the central high-pT efficiency by ~10 percentage points relative to the public measurement.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_lowpt
coefficients.locator: Fig 2(c) forward region 1.5<|eta|<2.5 (eff vs eta, pT>500 MeV); Fig 2(d) low-pT region
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.65-0.78 in forward eta (Fig 2c: ~0.80 at |eta|=1.5 falling to ~0.65 at |eta|=2.5, local rise to ~0.76 near |eta|=2.2); folding in low-pT (pT<1 GeV) reduces this. Card bin 0.1-1.0 GeV partly below measured 0.5 GeV range.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~1.5% syst in most-forward region (Sec 6.3); efficiency-correction uncertainty 0.4% for |eta|>1.5
coefficients.proposed_revision: ~0.68 +/- 0.05 (forward, low-pT estimate). Rationale: card's 0.60 is slightly low vs the ~0.65-0.78 forward band, but the 0.1-0.5 GeV sub-range is unmeasured and forward low-pT efficiency is lower, so 0.60 is a defensible conservative bin-average.
coefficients.rationale: Read from Fig 2(c): forward efficiency spans ~0.65-0.80; with the unmeasured 0.1-0.5 GeV part dragging the average down, 0.60 is plausible but not directly confirmable for this exact bin.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_highpt
coefficients.locator: Fig 2(c) forward region 1.5<|eta|<2.5 (eff vs eta, integrated pT>500 MeV); Fig 2(d) plateau
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.70-0.78: Fig 2(c) shows 1.5<|eta|<2.5 efficiency falling from ~0.80 (|eta|=1.5) to ~0.65 (|eta|=2.5) with local bump ~0.76 near |eta|=2.2; eta-averaged forward ~0.72-0.75
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~1.5% syst (most-forward region, Sec 6.3 / p.11); total eff uncertainty up to 1.4% (eta)
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.73 +/- 0.04 (forward eta-averaged, pT>1 GeV, from Fig 2c). Rationale: card's 0.85 is ~0.10-0.12 (about 12-14%) HIGHER than the measured forward efficiency of ~0.72-0.75; the card is optimistic, as forward tracking suffers larger material losses (efficiency ~0.65-0.78, not 0.85).
coefficients.rationale: Fig 2(c): measured forward (1.5<|eta|<2.5) efficiency is ~0.65-0.80 (eta-average ~0.73), well below the card's 0.85. The card overstates forward high-pT efficiency by ~0.10-0.12.

coefficients.name: eff_eta_above_2p5
coefficients.locator: Fig 2(c) / Sec 3: measurement and ID acceptance limited to |eta|<2.5
coefficients.extracted_value: 0 (ATLAS inner detector tracking acceptance ends at |eta|=2.5; no charged-particle tracks reconstructed beyond)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: The ATLAS Run-2 ID tracking acceptance is |eta|<2.5 (paper restricts to |eta|<2.5 throughout). Zero efficiency beyond |eta|=2.5 correctly encodes this geometric acceptance limit.

extractions.source_summary: Primary measured source for the EM barrel: ATLAS Collaboration (M. Aharrouche et al.), "Energy linearity and resolution of the ATLAS electromagnetic barrel calorimeter in an electron test-beam," Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A597 (2008) 178; arXiv:physics/0608012 — already cited in the card. Fig. 19 gives a single-cell (eta=0.687, phi=0.28) fit with sampling term 10.1 +/- 0.1 %.sqrt(GeV) and local constant term 0.17 +/- 0.04 %, using the form sigma/E = sampling/sqrt(E) (+) constant (+) noise/E. Design/target form (a~10%, b~170 MeV noise, c=0.7%) given in ATLAS LAr readiness paper, arXiv:0912.2642 (Eur. Phys. J. C70 (2010) 723), Eq. (1) and Sec. 2.1; the GLOBAL constant term measured there is c~0.5% (EM barrel) / 0.7% (endcap) (Sec. 3.4.4), larger than the card's 0.17%. Definitive corroboration of BOTH the card barrel and FCal numbers with the identical functional form (sigma_E/E = a/sqrt(E/GeV) (+) c, no noise term): ATLAS Collaboration, "AtlFast3: the next generation of fast simulation in ATLAS," Comput. Softw. Big Sci. 6 (2022) 7; arXiv:2109.02551, Table 4 (Eq. 3): "LAr EM barrel and endcap" a=10.1%, c=0.2%; "FCal" a=28.5%, c=3.5%. These are collaboration-endorsed intrinsic-resolution values and match the card to <=0.03% absolute. Note: the JINST 3 S08003 ATLAS detector paper (cited in the card comment as jinst8_08_s08003 / physics/0608012) is the canonical detector reference but its FCal table could not be fetched (jinst.sissa.it blocked by egress policy 403); the AtlFast3 Table 4 supersedes it as the authoritative numeric source for these exact coefficients.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card splits at |eta|=3.2 into EM (|eta|<=3.2) and FCal (3.2<|eta|<=4.9). AtlFast3 Table 4 / ATLAS geometry: LAr EM barrel+endcap covers |eta|<3.2 (EMB |eta|<1.475, EMEC 1.375<|eta|<3.2), FCal covers 3.1<|eta|<4.9 (slight 3.1-3.2 overlap region). The card's single EM term for all |eta|<=3.2 lumps barrel and endcap together using the barrel-measured 10.1%/0.17% — the endcap stochastic term is actually somewhat larger and eta-dependent, and the physics/0608012 measurement is a SINGLE barrel cell at eta=0.687, not an eta-binned map. Card upper FCal edge 4.9 matches FCal coverage; card omits the noise (N) term that the design form (0912.2642 Eq.1, b~170 MeV) includes, consistent with the AtlFast3 simplified form which also drops noise.

coefficients.name: S_em_barrel_endcap (stochastic, |eta|<=3.2)
coefficients.applicability: ECAL EM, |eta|<=3.2 (barrel+endcap lumped), all pt; source measurement at single barrel cell eta=0.687
coefficients.locator: physics/0608012 Fig. 19 (Sampl. term box: 10.1 +/- 0.1) ; arXiv:2109.02551 Table 4 row 'LAr EM barrel and endcap' a=10.1%
coefficients.extracted_value: 10.1 %.sqrt(GeV)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Card 0.101 = 10.1% exactly matches the physics/0608012 Fig.19 fitted sampling term (10.1+/-0.1) and AtlFast3 Table 4 (10.1%); same sqrt(E) functional form. Caveat: value is barrel-cell-specific but applied to full |eta|<=3.2.

coefficients.name: C_em_barrel_endcap (constant, |eta|<=3.2)
coefficients.applicability: ECAL EM, |eta|<=3.2, high-energy plateau of resolution; source = LOCAL constant term at barrel cell eta=0.687

extractions.source_summary: ATLAS Collaboration, "Electron reconstruction and identification in the ATLAS experiment using the 2015 and 2016 LHC proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV", Eur. Phys. J. C 79 (2019) 639, DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-019-7140-6, arXiv:1902.04655 (CERN-EP-2018-273). Authoritative ATLAS collaboration measurement of the likelihood-based electron identification (LH-ID) operating-point efficiencies in Run 2. Section 6.3 (p.~23) states target ID efficiencies at ET = 40 GeV are 93% (Loose), 88% (Medium), 80% (Tight). Section 6.3 also gives ET dependence: Loose ranges 85% at ET=20 GeV to 96% at ET=100 GeV; Tight 55% at ET=4.5 GeV to 90% at ET=100 GeV. Figure 8 (top: efficiency vs ET; bottom: efficiency vs eta) shows the measured efficiencies over the precision region |eta|<2.47 for Loose/Medium/Tight, excluding 1.37<|eta|<1.52, ET>4.5 GeV. NOTE: the card's flat per-WP efficiency does not correspond to a single tabulated ATLAS number; the closest match for the central 0.95 value is the Loose WP plateau (~93-96% at high ET).

coefficients.name: eff_lowpt_pt_le_10
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.3 text (p.23, lines ~942-946 and 1019-1028) and Fig. 8 (top, efficiency vs ET). ID efficiency measured down to ET=4.5 GeV.
coefficients.extracted_value: Non-zero at pT<10 GeV: Loose ~85% at ET=20 GeV and lower toward ET=4.5 GeV; Tight 55% at ET=4.5 GeV. Efficiency is NOT zero below 10 GeV; it falls smoothly with decreasing ET.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: Loose (Tight) total uncertainty 3% (4%) at ET=4.5 GeV
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current as a fiducial pT>10 GeV analysis threshold, but document it as an analysis-level pT cut, not a measured efficiency. If a turn-on is desired, ATLAS measures finite efficiency (~85% Loose) already at ET=20 GeV down to 4.5 GeV.
coefficients.rationale: The 0.00 below 10 GeV is a hard analysis pT threshold (a modelling choice), not the measured efficiency, which is finite below 10 GeV per Sec 6.3 / Fig 8. As a fiducial cut it is acceptable; as a 'reco efficiency' it is not what the source measures.

coefficients.name: eff_central_pt_gt_10
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.3, p.23, line 946 (target eff at ET=40 GeV) and lines 1026-1027; Fig. 8 top (eff vs ET) and bottom (eff vs eta).
coefficients.extracted_value: Loose WP: 93% at ET=40 GeV, rising to 96% at ET=100 GeV (85% at ET=20 GeV). Medium WP: 88% at 40 GeV. Tight WP: 80% at 40 GeV. Eta dependence (Fig 8 bottom) roughly flat across barrel ~90-96% with a dip in 1.37<|eta|<1.52.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: Loose total uncertainty ~0.1% at ET=40 GeV (3% at ET=4.5 GeV); plateau spread ~93-96% over ET=40-100 GeV
coefficients.proposed_revision: Revise to 0.93 +/- 0.02 if targeting the Loose WP (ATLAS Loose plateau is 93% at 40 GeV, up to 96% at 100 GeV); or 0.88 for Medium, 0.80 for Tight. Current 0.95 is slightly optimistic for Loose (above the 93% target, near the 100 GeV value).
coefficients.rationale: Card 0.95 lies between the Loose plateau target (93%) and the high-ET value (96%), so it is mildly optimistic for Loose and substantially optimistic for Medium (88%) or Tight (80%). The single flat value also ignores the measured pT turn-on. Closest consistent WP is Loose at high ET.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_pt_gt_10
coefficients.locator: Fig. 8 bottom (efficiency vs eta, Loose/Medium/Tight) over |eta|<2.47; transition region 1.37<|eta|<1.52 excluded; Sec 6.3 text lines 946, 1026-1027.
coefficients.extracted_value: ATLAS does not report a flat 85% in the endcap. Fig 8 shows the Loose efficiency in the endcap (1.52<|eta|<2.47) broadly comparable to the barrel (~88-94%), with a localized dip near the transition region (1.37-1.52) where the measurement is excluded. No abrupt step down to 85% at |eta|=1.5.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: total uncertainties small (sub-percent to few-percent), eta-bin-dependent; transition region dips to ~85% or below
coefficients.proposed_revision: Revise toward ~0.90 +/- 0.03 for the endcap if targeting Loose WP. The 0.85 is a crude conservative approximation; the real eta structure is a roughly flat ~90% Loose efficiency with a localized transition-region dip near |eta|~1.45, not a clean 0.95->0.85 step at |eta|=1.5.
coefficients.rationale: Measured endcap Loose efficiency (~88-94%, Fig 8 bottom) is higher than the card's flat 0.85; the 0.85 is conservative for the endcap and the 0.95->0.85 step at |eta|=1.5 does not match the actual eta profile (dip is in the 1.37-1.52 transition region). For Medium/Tight the 0.85 would instead be optimistic.

coefficients.name: eff_outer_eta_gt_25
coefficients.locator: Sec 1/6 acceptance statements (lines 129, 276, 405, 699): precision/identification region is |eta| < 2.47; central-electron ID defined only up to |eta|<2.47.
coefficients.extracted_value: Electron reconstruction+identification in the central detector is defined and measured only for |eta| < 2.47; above that the LH-ID is not provided (forward electrons use a separate algorithm not covered here).
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.00 above |eta|=2.5 is correct in spirit), but note the precise ATLAS ID acceptance edge is |eta|=2.47, not 2.5.
coefficients.rationale: Setting efficiency to 0 outside the central-electron acceptance is consistent with the source, which defines LH-ID only for |eta|<2.47. The card's 2.5 boundary slightly over-extends the true 2.47 edge (minor binning mismatch).

extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card eta binning is a coarse 2-bin form (|eta|<=1.5, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5) with a sharp 0.95->0.85 step at |eta|=1.5 and a cutoff at |eta|=2.5. The ATLAS source (arXiv:1902.04655) defines ID over |eta|<2.47 in fine cluster-eta bins {0.0,0.6,0.8,1.15,1.37,1.52,1.81,2.01,2.37,2.47} (Table 2 / line 933) and excludes the transition region 1.37<|eta|<1.52. The card's step at |eta|=1.5 has no counterpart in the data (the real feature is a localized dip in the 1.37-1.52 transition region), and the card's 2.5 outer edge should be 2.47. pT binning: card uses a single flat value above a hard 10 GeV turn-on with 0 below; the source measures a smooth ET turn-on from 4.5 GeV (Loose ~85% at 20 GeV rising to 96% at 100 GeV) in ET bins (Table 3), so the card's flat-plus-hard-cut form does not reproduce the measured ET dependence.

extractions.source_summary: Authoritative source: ATLAS Collaboration, "Electron and photon energy calibration with the ATLAS detector using LHC Run 1 data", Eur. Phys. J. C 74 (2014) 3071, arXiv:1407.5063. This is the collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed measurement of the ATLAS electron/photon energy resolution. Eq. (2) gives the EM-calorimeter resolution form sigma_E/E = a/sqrt(E) (+) b/E (+) c with a (sampling) = (9-10)%/sqrt(E[GeV]) at low |eta|, b (noise) = 350*cosh(eta) MeV per 3x7 cluster at mu=20, and c (constant term) design 0.7%. The measured effective constant term from Z->ee (Fig. 27, Sect. 9) is ~0.7% for |eta|<0.6, 0.7-1.5% over most of the acceptance, ~3.5% in the barrel/endcap transition 1.37<|eta|<1.52, and ~2.5% for |eta|>2.3; resolution corrections are ~0.8% (barrel) / ~1% (endcap) on average. Fig. 35 (|eta|=0.2) shows the electron resolution curve: sigma_E/E ~1.2-1.3% at ET=40 GeV rising slowly to ~1.5% near 200 GeV. The companion higher-stat Run-2 calibration is arXiv:1908.00005 / 1902.04655 (consistent picture). NOTE: electrons in ATLAS are calorimeter-dominated, so the physically correct resolution IMPROVES with energy toward the constant term; the Delphes tracker form sqrt(a^2+(b*pt)^2) used here DEGRADES with pt and is the wrong functional structure for electrons.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card uses 3 bins: |eta|<=0.5, 0.5-1.5, 1.5-2.5. The ATLAS measurement (arXiv:1407.5063 Fig. 27/35) is given finely in |eta| with key boundaries at 0.6, 1.37, 1.52, 1.82, 2.3 (driven by barrel/endcap/transition calorimeter geometry). In particular the card's middle bin 0.5-1.5 straddles the barrel/endcap transition crack (1.37-1.52) where c jumps to ~3.5%, and the card's outer bin 1.5-2.5 lumps together the ~1% endcap region (1.52-2.3) with the ~2.5% high-eta region (>2.3). Card binning does not match the source binning; a single (a,b) per coarse bin cannot reproduce the transition-region behaviour. Functional-form mismatch is more serious than binning: the card has no 1/sqrt(E) sampling term at all.

coefficients.name: a_eta0_05 (electron const term, |eta|<=0.5)
coefficients.current_value: 0.03 (i.e. 3% constant relative resolution; full term in sqrt: 0.03^2)
coefficients.applicability: electron, |eta|<=0.5, pt>0.1 GeV; constant (pt-independent) term of sigma_pt/pt
coefficients.locator: Eq. (2); constant term c: Fig. 27 and Sect. 9 (effective c ~0.7% for |eta|<0.6); resolution curve Fig. 35 (|eta|=0.2, sigma_E/E ~1.2-1.3% at ET=40 GeV)
coefficients.extracted_value: Effective constant term c ~ 0.007 (0.7%) for |eta|<0.6; total sigma_E/E ~0.012-0.013 at ET=40 GeV (plot-read from Fig. 35)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: delta_c (total) ~ +/-0.001 (Fig. 27 bottom); measurement of c gives ~5% relative resolution uncertainty at ET=40 GeV (Sect. 9.2)
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.007 +/- 0.001 (use measured effective constant term ~0.7%); ideally also add a sampling term a_samp~0.10/sqrt(E) and drop/zero the b*pt term -- but within the current sqrt(a^2+(b*pt)^2) form the asymptotic value should be ~0.007, not 0.03
coefficients.rationale: Card 3% constant term is ~4x larger than the ATLAS measured effective constant term (~0.7%); at pt=40 GeV the card gives sigma_pt/pt = sqrt(0.03^2+(1.3e-3*40)^2) ~6.0% vs measured ~1.2-1.3%. Value extracted from Fig. 27/Fig. 35 of 1407.5063.

coefficients.name: b_eta0_05 (electron pt-slope term, |eta|<=0.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, |eta|<=0.5; coefficient of the linear-in-pt (b*pt) growth of sigma_pt/pt
coefficients.locator: Eq. (2) (no linear b*E term exists for EM calo); Fig. 35 shows sigma_E/E essentially FLAT/slightly falling vs ET, not rising linearly
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated -- ATLAS EM-calo electron resolution has NO term that grows linearly with energy; it falls as 1/sqrt(E) toward the constant term
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0 (remove the b*pt term for electrons; it is a tracker parametrization copied from charged hadrons and contradicts calorimeter physics). If retained, the high-pt resolution is grossly overestimated.
coefficients.rationale: The b*pt term makes electron resolution worsen with pt (e.g. 13% at pt=100 GeV from this term alone), but ATLAS electrons are calorimeter-measured and resolution IMPROVES with energy (Fig. 35). This coefficient (identical to the charged-hadron value) reflects the wrong functional form, not a measured number; no public source supports a linearly growing electron resolution.

coefficients.name: a_eta05_15 (electron const term, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5, pt>0.1 GeV; constant term of sigma_pt/pt. NB this bin straddles the barrel/endcap transition crack 1.37-1.52
coefficients.locator: Fig. 27 / Sect. 9: effective c ~0.7-1.5% over most acceptance, jumping to ~3.5% in transition 1.37<|eta|<1.52; resolution corrections ~0.8% barrel
coefficients.extracted_value: c ~ 0.008-0.015 for the non-transition part of this bin; c ~ 0.035 only in the narrow crack 1.37<|eta|<1.52
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.012 +/- 0.003 for the bulk of the bin (split out a separate 1.37-1.52 crack bin with c~0.035 if higher fidelity is desired); current 0.05 overstates the bulk constant term
coefficients.rationale: Card 5% constant term exceeds the measured ~0.8-1.5% over most of 0.5-1.5; only the narrow 1.37-1.52 crack reaches ~3.5%. A single 0.05 is too pessimistic for the bin as a whole and cannot represent the sharp transition feature. Values from Fig. 27 of 1407.5063.

coefficients.name: b_eta05_15 (electron pt-slope term, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5; coefficient of linear-in-pt growth of sigma_pt/pt
coefficients.locator: Eq. (2); Fig. 35 (no linearly rising term in EM-calo resolution)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated -- no linear-in-energy term in the ATLAS EM calorimeter electron resolution
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0 (remove for electrons; calorimeter resolution falls as 1/sqrt(E)). Value is a charged-hadron tracker coefficient, not an electron measurement.
coefficients.rationale: Same functional-form problem as the |eta|<0.5 b term: a linearly growing electron resolution contradicts the measured calorimeter behaviour in Fig. 35 of 1407.5063. No public source supports this coefficient for electrons.

coefficients.name: a_eta15_25 (electron const term, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>0.1 GeV; constant term of sigma_pt/pt. Bin spans endcap (1.52-2.3, c~1%) and high-eta (>2.3, c~2.5%)
coefficients.locator: Fig. 27 / Sect. 9: effective c ~1% in endcap (1.52-2.3), ~2.5% for |eta|>2.3; resolution corrections ~1% in endcap on average
coefficients.extracted_value: c ~ 0.010 for 1.52-2.3; c ~ 0.025 for |eta|>2.3 (plus larger sampling term at high |eta| due to upstream material)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: delta_c (total) ~ +/-0.002-0.003 (Fig. 27 bottom; endcap less well constrained)
coefficients.proposed_revision: ~0.015 +/- 0.005 (acceptance-averaged endcap effective constant term); 0.15 is ~10x the measured value. Note sampling term in endcap is larger (>11%/sqrt(E)) but still falls with E.
coefficients.rationale: Card 15% constant term is roughly an order of magnitude above the ATLAS measured endcap effective constant term (~1%, up to ~2.5% beyond |eta|=2.3). The card value is grossly pessimistic; extracted from Fig. 27 of 1407.5063.

coefficients.name: b_eta15_25 (electron pt-slope term, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5; coefficient of linear-in-pt growth of sigma_pt/pt
coefficients.locator: Eq. (2); Fig. 35 (EM-calo resolution has no linear-in-energy growth)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated -- no linear-in-energy term in ATLAS electron calorimeter resolution
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0 (remove for electrons). Coefficient is the charged-hadron tracker value; for endcap electrons the dominant pt dependence is the FALLING 1/sqrt(E) sampling term (>11%/sqrt(E)), not a rising b*pt term.
coefficients.rationale: A b*pt term gives sigma~31% at pt=100 GeV from this term alone, which contradicts the measured improvement of calorimeter resolution with energy (Fig. 35). The number is a tracker parametrization with no electron-resolution source.

extractions.source_summary: ATLAS Collaboration, "Electron reconstruction and identification in the ATLAS experiment using the 2015 and 2016 LHC proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV", Eur. Phys. J. C 79 (2019) 639, arXiv:1902.04655. Authoritative collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed (EPJC) Run-2 e/gamma performance paper. Relevant content: Section 5 + Figure 2 (top): track-fitting-step reconstruction efficiency ranges from ~80% at ET=1 GeV to >98% above ET=10 GeV; total reconstruction efficiency <60% below 4.5 GeV due to the ET>2.5 GeV cluster-seed requirement. Figure 9 and Conclusions: the reconstruction efficiency relative to reconstructed clusters (epsilon_reco) ranges 96%-99% for ET>15 GeV over the full |eta|<2.47 acceptance; data uncertainty ~1% in 15-20 GeV bin, per-mille at higher ET; below 15 GeV taken from simulation with 2% (barrel)/5% (endcap) assigned uncertainty. NOTE: paper covers |eta|<2.47 only and bins by barrel/endcap (transition ~1.37-1.52), not the card's 1.5/2.5 split; it does NOT tabulate a separate low-efficiency forward plateau for epsilon_reco (Fig 9 shows ~96-99% across full eta for ET>15 GeV).
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card uses |eta|<=1.5, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, |eta|>2.5. Source (1902.04655) is defined only for |eta|<2.47 (card's 2.5 cutoff slightly exceeds measured acceptance) and bins efficiencies as barrel vs endcap with the EM-calorimeter transition crack at ~1.37-1.52 (close to card's 1.5 boundary, acceptable). Card pt bins (0.1-1, 1-100, >100 GeV) do not match source ET bins (ET=1, 10, 15-20, 25-30, 40-45, 80-150 GeV); the source epsilon_reco plateau (96-99%) covers ET>15 GeV with no separate >100 GeV value, and the lowest card bin (0.1-1 GeV) lies entirely below the source's 4.5 GeV reconstruction threshold and is unconstrained there.

coefficients.name: eff_pt_below_0p1
coefficients.locator: n/a (structural low-pt cutoff in Delphes formula)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Structural cutoff: electrons with pt<=0.1 GeV are dropped. Not a measured efficiency; no source needed. The paper's reconstruction is defined only for ET>4.5 GeV, so a value of 0 well below that range is harmless.

coefficients.name: eff_central_lowpt

coefficients.rationale: This bin (0.1-1 GeV) is entirely below the paper's 4.5 GeV reconstruction validity range; the cluster seed requires ET>2.5 GeV so total reco eff is <60% below 4.5 GeV. No measurement exists at pt<1 GeV, so the card's 0.73 has no authoritative source and appears optimistic relative to the <60% statement.

coefficients.locator: Conclusions p.40: 'For ET>15 GeV, the reconstruction efficiencies range from 96% to 99%'; Fig.9 (barrel, ET 15-150 GeV ~0.97-0.99); Sec.5.2: track-fit step >98% above ET=10 GeV

coefficients.rationale: Measured central epsilon_reco is 96-99% for ET>15 GeV (Fig.9, Conclusions); the card's 0.95 sits just below this. It is defensible as an average over the wide 1-100 GeV bin including lower-efficiency 1-15 GeV, but ~0.97 better reflects the plateau.

coefficients.locator: Conclusions p.40 (reco eff up to 99% for ET>15 GeV); Fig.9 panel '80 GeV < ET < 150 GeV' (barrel ~0.99); Sec.5.2 (track-fit step >98% above 10 GeV)

coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: The source quotes the upper end of epsilon_reco as 99% for ET>15 GeV, and Fig.9 shows the barrel plateau ~0.99 in the 80-150 GeV bin; the card's 0.99 for pt>100 GeV is consistent. Caveat: source's highest bin extends only to ~150 GeV; plateau assumed flat above.

coefficients.locator: Fig.2(top) caption (<60% below 4.5 GeV, total reco eff); no dedicated forward sub-GeV measurement
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (bin entirely below 4.5 GeV reconstruction range; no forward sub-GeV measurement exists)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.50) as engineering estimate; flag unconstrained. No source measures forward-region efficiency below 1 GeV.
coefficients.rationale: The 0.1-1 GeV forward bin lies entirely below the paper's 4.5 GeV reconstruction validity threshold and the endcap is not separately measured at sub-GeV ET; the card's 0.50 has no authoritative source.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_midpt
coefficients.locator: Conclusions p.40 (reco eff 96-99% for ET>15 GeV, full |eta|<2.47); Fig.9 (endcap |eta|~1.5-2.47, panels 15-150 GeV, ~0.96-0.99); endcap MC uncertainty 5% below 15 GeV
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.96-0.99 for ET>15 GeV in the endcap (epsilon_reco; Fig.9 y-range 0.96-1.02 across full eta); lower below 15 GeV
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~1% (data, 15-20 GeV) -> per-mille high ET; 5% (endcap) MC-assigned below 15 GeV

coefficients.rationale: Source epsilon_reco (relative to cluster) is 96-99% across full |eta|<2.47 for ET>15 GeV (Fig.9 shows no large barrel/endcap gap); the card's 0.83 is well below this. The card value likely folds in additional cluster-finding/crack/acceptance losses, but relative to the measured reconstruction efficiency it is card-pessimistic.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_highpt
coefficients.locator: Conclusions p.40 (reco eff up to 99%, full |eta|<2.47); Fig.9 panel '80 GeV < ET < 150 GeV' (endcap |eta|~1.5-2.47 ~0.97-0.99)
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.97-0.99 (epsilon_reco plateau, endcap, high ET, Fig.9)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Revise to ~0.97 +/- 0.02 (endcap, pt>100 GeV). Fig.9 shows the endcap plateau ~0.97-0.99 at high ET, above the card's 0.90; if extra acceptance/crack losses are intended, document them, otherwise raise toward ~0.97.
coefficients.rationale: Measured endcap epsilon_reco at high ET is ~0.97-0.99 (Fig.9, 80-150 GeV panel); the card's 0.90 is lower and appears card-pessimistic unless deliberately absorbing additional forward acceptance/crack inefficiencies beyond the cluster-relative measurement.

extractions.source_summary: The HCal ResolutionFormula (lines 360-362) spans THREE distinct ATLAS hadronic calorimeters, but the card cites only ONE source. (1) |eta|<=1.7 = Tile barrel (scintillator/iron). Card comment cites Y. Kulchitsky et al., "Hadron Energy Reconstruction for the ATLAS Barrel Prototype Combined Calorimeter in the Framework of the Non-parametrical Method," hep-ex/0004009 (NIM A480 (2002) 508), which reports combined (LAr-EM + Tile-had) resolution sigma/E = (58+/-3)%/sqrt(E) (+) (2.5+/-0.3)% (+) (1.7+/-0.2) GeV/E. Standalone TileCal test-beam pion resolution is ~52%/sqrt(E) (+) ~3% (multiple TileCal proceedings, e.g. ATL-TILECAL-PROC-2015-002), which matches the card's stochastic term better than the cited combined value. (2) 1.7<|eta|<=3.2 = LAr Hadronic End-Cap (HEC): authoritative source is ATLAS HEC Collaboration (D.M. Gingrich et al.), "The ATLAS liquid argon hadronic end-cap calorimeter: construction and selected beam test results," physics/0407026 (NIM A540 (2005) 392), reporting pion sigma/E = (78+/-2)%/sqrt(E) (+) (5.0+/-0.3)%. (3) 3.2<|eta|<=4.9 = LAr Forward Calorimeter (FCal): authoritative source is A. Artamonov et al., "The ATLAS Forward Calorimeter," JINST 3 (2008) P02010, reporting beam-test charged-pion sigma/E = 94%/sqrt(E) (+) 7.5%. The single cited paper (hep-ex/0004009) is authoritative ONLY for the central Tile region; the HEC and FCal coefficients have no source in the card and must cite physics/0407026 and JINST 3 P02010 respectively.

extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: The card's three eta bins (|eta|<=1.7, 1.7-3.2, 3.2-4.9) correspond to three PHYSICALLY DISTINCT ATLAS calorimeters (Tile barrel/extended-barrel; LAr HEC; LAr FCal), each with its own test-beam reference. The single cited source hep-ex/0004009 is a Tile barrel prototype paper and is NOT a valid source for the 1.7-3.2 (HEC) or 3.2-4.9 (FCal) bins. Additionally, the card boundary at |eta|=1.7 lumps the Tile extended barrel and the Tile/LAr transition together; real ATLAS Tile coverage is |eta|<1.7 with the LAr HEC spanning 1.5<|eta|<3.2 and FCal 3.1<|eta|<4.9, so the 1.7 split is an approximation. The cited hep-ex/0004009 value is for a COMBINED LAr-EM+Tile module (58/2.5/1.7), whereas the central card numbers (52.05/3.02/1.59) align better with Tile STANDALONE, an additional definitional mismatch.

extractions.source_summary: Primary JES authority: ATLAS Collaboration, "Jet energy scale measurements and their systematic uncertainties in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector," Phys. Rev. D 96 (2017) 072002, arXiv:1703.09665. Central (|eta|<1.2) in-situ JES uncertainty ~4.5% at pT=20 GeV falling to <1% for 100-500 GeV; forward up to ~2%. Primary JER authority: ATLAS Collaboration, "Jet energy scale and resolution measured in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector," Eur. Phys. J. C 81 (2021) 689, arXiv:2007.02645 (Eq. 4: sigma(pT)/pT = N/pT (+) S/sqrt(pT) (+) C; measured relative resolution (24+/-1.5)% at 20 GeV to (6+/-0.5)% at 300 GeV; Figs. 29-30, central 0.2<=|eta|<0.7). Jet-definition-matched reference (anti-kt R=0.6, identical to card's ParameterR 0.6): ATLAS Collaboration, "Jet energy resolution in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV recorded in 2010 with the ATLAS detector," Eur. Phys. J. C 73 (2013) 2306, arXiv:1210.6210 (Eq. resolution N(+)S/sqrt(pT)(+)C, Figs. 8 and 13, |y|<0.8). NOTE: the card uses a Delphes 'EnergyScale' (multiplicative) module, not a 'Smearing' module, so the formula is a fractional energy-SCALE factor, not directly sigma/pT; this mismatch is central to the verdicts below.

coefficients.name: jes_stochastic_coeff_eta0 (the 3.0 in (3.0-0.2*abs(eta))^2)
coefficients.current_value: 3.0 (units sqrt(GeV); appears squared as 9.0 GeV in numerator of S^2/pt)
coefficients.applicability: eta=0 value of the eta-dependent coefficient; whole-jet, pt in GeV; anti-kt R=0.6 jets (ParameterR 0.6, JetPTMin 20 GeV)
coefficients.locator: arXiv:2007.02645 Eq.(4) and Fig.30(a) (relative JER vs pT, 0.2<=|eta|<0.7); abstract quote (24+/-1.5)% at 20 GeV, (6+/-0.5)% at 300 GeV. Cross-check arXiv:1210.6210 Fig.8/Fig.13 (anti-kt R=0.6, |y|<0.8).
coefficients.extracted_value: Implied ATLAS central stochastic term S ~ 0.6-0.9 sqrt(GeV) (plot-read: resolution ~12% at 60 GeV gives S~0.9; ~6% at 300 GeV with C~0.04-0.05 gives S~0.7). The card's coefficient 3.0 corresponds, IF interpreted as sigma/pt = S/sqrt(pt), to S=3.0 sqrt(GeV) i.e. 30% at 100 GeV -- about 3-5x the measured central JER. As an ENERGY-SCALE factor sqrt(1+9/pt), it produces a +15% upward energy bias at 20 GeV, +4.5% at 100 GeV, vs ATLAS JES non-closure calibrated to ~+/-4.5% (20 GeV) and <1% (100 GeV).
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: JER S term central ~ +/-0.05 sqrt(GeV) (from (6+/-0.5)% at 300 GeV, (24+/-1.5)% at 20 GeV); JES uncertainty ~4.5% (20 GeV) to <1% (100-500 GeV)
coefficients.proposed_revision: If module kept as EnergyScale (mean JES non-closure): replace with ~1.0 (ATLAS jets are calibrated to unity within <1-4.5%), i.e. effectively no scale shift; document JES uncertainty separately. If the intent is JER smearing, move to a JetResolution/Smearing module with sigma/pt = sqrt((0.06)^2 + (0.8)^2/pt + (2.0)^2/pt^2) (S~0.8 sqrt(GeV), central), per arXiv:2007.02645 Fig.30. Either way the bare value 3.0 is not supported as a scale coefficient.
coefficients.rationale: Read verbatim from line 633: coefficient 3.0 inside (3.0-0.2*abs(eta))^2. Applied in an EnergyScale module it yields a +4.5% to +15% upward energy bias over pT 100->20 GeV, whereas ATLAS calibrates the JES mean to unity (non-closure <1-4.5%); interpreted as a stochastic JER term S=3.0 sqrt(GeV) it is 3-5x the measured central S~0.7-0.9 sqrt(GeV). No source supports 3.0; it is a legacy/illustrative number.

coefficients.name: jes_eta_slope (the 0.2 in 0.2*abs(eta))
coefficients.current_value: 0.2 (units sqrt(GeV) per unit |eta|; reduces the stochastic coefficient from 3.0 at eta=0 to 2.0 at |eta|=2.5)
coefficients.applicability: eta-dependence of the coefficient over the jet acceptance |eta|<~2.8 (card JetPTMin 20, PartonEtaMax 2.5); anti-kt R=0.6
coefficients.locator: arXiv:1210.6210 Fig.13 (R=0.6, four rapidity bins |y|<0.8, 0.8<=|y|<1.2, 1.2<=|y|<2.1, 2.1<=|y|<2.8) and Fig.8; arXiv:2007.02645 Fig.30(b) (relative JER vs |eta| at pT=30 GeV).
coefficients.extracted_value: ATLAS JER degrades (does NOT improve) toward the transition/endcap and then varies; central |y|<0.8 resolution ~12% at 60 GeV, rising at 1.2<|y|<2.1 (transition) before forward. The card's monotonic DECREASE of the coefficient with |eta| (better resolution forward) has the wrong qualitative trend versus arXiv:1210.6210 Fig.13 / arXiv:2007.02645 Fig.30(b), where resolution worsens through the barrel-endcap transition (~1.2<|eta|<1.7).
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: eta-dependence not given as a single slope in the sources; per-bin resolution uncertainties ~5-10% relative (arXiv:1210.6210 Sec.10)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Do not use a single linear -0.2*|eta| slope. Replace with eta-binned coefficients matching the source bins (|y|<0.8, 0.8-1.2, 1.2-2.1, 2.1-2.8 from arXiv:1210.6210 Fig.13, or 0.2<=|eta|<0.7 plus forward from arXiv:2007.02645 Fig.30b); the central->forward trend should worsen through the transition, not improve.
coefficients.rationale: Read verbatim from line 633 (0.2*abs(eta)). The implied trend (resolution/scale-bias improving with |eta|) contradicts the measured ATLAS eta dependence (arXiv:1210.6210 Fig.13, arXiv:2007.02645 Fig.30b), where JER worsens through the calorimeter transition region; no source supports a -0.2 sqrt(GeV)/|eta| linear slope.

coefficients.name: jes_constant_asymptote (the +1.0 additive term inside sqrt)
coefficients.current_value: 1.0 (dimensionless; makes the scale factor -> sqrt(1.0)=1.0 as pt->infinity, i.e. C^2=1 with C=1 representing the unity high-pT scale, NOT a fractional constant term)
coefficients.applicability: high-pt asymptote of the multiplicative scale factor, all eta; anti-kt R=0.6
coefficients.locator: arXiv:2007.02645 Eq.(4) C term (constant term, dominates above ~400 GeV) and Fig.30(a); arXiv:1703.09665 (high-pT central JES non-closure <1%).
coefficients.extracted_value: The +1.0 here is the SCALE asymptote (factor->1, correct: ATLAS high-pT jets are scale-calibrated to unity within <1%, arXiv:1703.09665). It is NOT the JER constant term C; the measured JER constant term in sigma/pt form is C ~ 0.04-0.05 (4-5%), reached above ~400 GeV (arXiv:2007.02645 Eq.4 text and Fig.30a).
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: high-pT JES non-closure <1% (arXiv:1703.09665); JER constant term C ~ 0.05 +/- 0.01 (arXiv:2007.02645)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (as the high-pT unity asymptote of an EnergyScale factor the value 1.0 is correct and physically required). If the module is converted to a JER Smearing, the constant term should instead be encoded as C~0.05 (NOT 1.0) inside sigma/pt = sqrt(C^2 + S^2/pt + N^2/pt^2).
coefficients.rationale: Read verbatim from line 633 (+1.0). For an EnergyScale module this 1.0 is the mandatory high-pT unity asymptote and matches ATLAS scale calibration to unity within <1% (arXiv:1703.09665); it is the only one of the three numbers that is physically correct in context, though it must not be confused with the JER constant term C~0.05.

extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Severe binning/definition mismatch. The card uses a single smooth analytic function of (eta, pt) with no eta bins. ATLAS sources are eta-binned: arXiv:1210.6210 Fig.13 uses |y|<0.8, 0.8<=|y|<1.2, 1.2<=|y|<2.1, 2.1<=|y|<2.8 (anti-kt R=0.6, matching the card's ParameterR 0.6); arXiv:2007.02645 uses 0.2<=|eta|<0.7 central reference plus |eta| up to 4.5 (anti-kt R=0.4). The card's linear -0.2*|eta| coefficient cannot represent the measured non-monotonic eta dependence (degradation through the 1.2<|eta|<1.7 transition). Additionally a definitional mismatch: the card is an EnergyScale (multiplicative mean shift) module, whereas the natural ATLAS-measured quantity with this sqrt(S^2/pt) structure is the jet energy RESOLUTION (a Gaussian smearing), so the formula is applied in the wrong module type.

extractions.source_summary: Primary: ATLAS Collaboration, "Muon reconstruction and identification efficiency in ATLAS using the full Run 2 pp collision data set at sqrt(s)=13 TeV", arXiv:2012.00578 (Eur. Phys. J. C 81 (2021) 578). This is the authoritative, collaboration-endorsed source: it defines the Loose/Medium/Tight working points, states the muon acceptance |eta|<2.7 (ID up to 2.5, extended 2.5<|eta|<2.7 with ME/SiF muons), and measures the Medium reconstruction+identification efficiency to exceed 98% for 0.1<|eta|<2.5 with pt>10 GeV (Sec. 7.1, Figs. 12-14). Secondary/historical: ATLAS Collaboration, "Muon reconstruction efficiency and momentum resolution of the ATLAS experiment in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV in 2010", arXiv:1404.4562 (Eur. Phys. J. C 74 (2014) 3130), which quotes average Combined (CB) muon reconstruction efficiency 0.928+/-0.002 (chain 1) and 0.958+/-0.001 (chain 2) (Sec. 5, around p.10; Fig. 5), the historically contemporaneous match for the Delphes default 0.95. The candidate arXiv:1603.05598 (13 TeV, 3.2 fb-1) corroborates: reconstruction efficiency "close to 99%" over |eta|<2.5, 5<pt<100 GeV (abstract). The card carries NO inline reference; audit_ATLAS.md line 30 marks this block "Source needed (ATLAS muon ID)".
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card uses two efficiency bins (|eta|<=1.5 and 1.5<|eta|<=2.7) plus a hard cutoff at |eta|>2.7. The ATLAS sources do NOT use a 1.5 boundary: the natural physics boundaries are |eta|=2.5 (edge of ID/CB coverage) and |eta|=2.7 (edge of MS/ME-SiF coverage). The card's outer boundary of 2.7 is correct and well-motivated (matches MS acceptance, arXiv:2012.00578 Sec.5.1.2). The internal 1.5 split is a Delphes simplification not present in the source; the measured Medium efficiency is roughly flat at >98% across the whole 0.1<|eta|<2.5 range (no step at 1.5). The card's pt turn-on at 10 GeV matches the source statement that efficiencies are stable for pt>10 GeV and drop below ~5 GeV (arXiv:2012.00578 Sec.7.1, Fig.12-13).

coefficients.name: eff_lowpt_threshold
coefficients.applicability: all |eta|, muon pt <= 10 GeV; reco_efficiency turn-on
coefficients.locator: Sec. 7.1 (text around 'For muon tracks with pt greater than 10 GeV, the efficiencies and the data/MC agreement are stable...the efficiencies drop significantly in the pt region below 5 GeV'), Figs. 12-13
coefficients.extracted_value: Not a hard zero in data: Medium efficiency is ~91% at pt=4 GeV rising to ~95% at pt=9 GeV and >=98% for pt>10 GeV. The source shows a gradual turn-on below ~10 GeV, not a step to zero.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: stat error bars small (<1%); turn-on shape from Fig.12-13
coefficients.proposed_revision: Keep current as a pragmatic modeling choice, but document that it is a simplification: ATLAS Medium efficiency is ~91-95% in 4-10 GeV, not 0. If low-pt muons matter, replace the hard 0 with a turn-on (e.g. ~0.90 for 4<pt<10). For pt>10 GeV the choice is sound.
coefficients.rationale: The card discards all muons with pt<=10 GeV; ATLAS actually reconstructs Medium muons with ~91-95% efficiency in 4-10 GeV. This is a deliberate conservative Delphes threshold, acceptable for high-pt analyses but pessimistic at low pt.

coefficients.name: eff_central
coefficients.applicability: muon, |eta| <= 1.5, pt > 10 GeV; central reco+ID efficiency
coefficients.locator: arXiv:2012.00578 Sec.7.1 ('The efficiency of the Loose and Medium criteria exceeds 98% for tracks with 0.1<|eta|<2.5', Figs.12-14); arXiv:1404.4562 Sec.5 ('average CB muon reconstruction efficiency is 0.928+/-0.002 for chain 1 and 0.958+/-0.001 for chain 2', Fig.5)
coefficients.extracted_value: >0.98 (Run 2 Medium WP, 13 TeV); 0.928-0.958 (CB muons, 7 TeV)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: Run 2: data/MC differences ~0.5% on average; 7 TeV CB: +/-0.001 to 0.002 (stat), few % syst
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.98 +/- 0.01 (to match modern ATLAS Medium WP, arXiv:2012.00578). Current 0.95 is acceptable but ~3% low vs Run 2; it matches the older 7 TeV CB-muon value, so keep-with-note is defensible if the card targets a CB-muon-like selection.
coefficients.rationale: Run 2 Medium WP exceeds 98% in the central region; the card's 0.95 is ~3% conservative. It does match the older 7 TeV combined-muon efficiency (~0.93-0.96), so it is not wrong, just dated/conservative. Recommend bumping to 0.98 with the 2012.00578 reference.

coefficients.name: eff_forward
coefficients.applicability: muon, 1.5 < |eta| <= 2.7, pt > 10 GeV; forward reco+ID efficiency (spans ID-covered 1.5-2.5 plus MS-only extension 2.5-2.7)
coefficients.locator: Sec.5.1.2 (Medium WP: CB+IO within |eta|<2.5, extended by ME/SiF muons in 2.5<|eta|<2.7); Sec.6.4 'The double-ratio method for the 2.5<|eta|<2.7 region'; Sec.7.1 ('exceeds 98% for 0.1<|eta|<2.5', Figs.12-14)
coefficients.extracted_value: >0.98 for the 1.5-2.5 sub-range (Medium WP); lower (no single % flat value tabulated) in the MS-only 2.5<|eta|<2.7 extension where only ME/SiF muons exist and efficiency degrades
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: 1.5-2.5: ~0.5% data/MC; 2.5-2.7: larger, measured via double-ratio with sizeable syst (PDF/background)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Split the bin to reflect physics: ~0.98 for 1.5<|eta|<=2.5 and ~0.85 (or lower) for 2.5<|eta|<=2.7. The single value 0.85 averages a high-efficiency ID region (>98%) with a degraded MS-only forward region, so it is too low for 1.5-2.5 and roughly right for 2.5-2.7.
coefficients.rationale: For 1.5<|eta|<2.5 ATLAS Medium efficiency is >98%, far above the card's 0.85; only the narrow MS-only 2.5-2.7 extension has ~0.85-level (or lower) efficiency. Lumping them into 0.85 is pessimistic for the dominant 1.5-2.5 range. No source tabulates a single 0.85 number for this combined bin (no exact match).

coefficients.name: eff_out_of_acceptance
coefficients.locator: Abstract and Sec.2/5.1.2: muon acceptance is |eta|<2.7 (MDT precision chambers cover |eta|<2.7; ME/SiF extension reaches |eta|=2.7)
coefficients.extracted_value: 0 (no muon reconstruction beyond |eta|=2.7)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: n/a (acceptance boundary, not a measured efficiency)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: ATLAS muon reconstruction is defined only within |eta|<2.7 (MS coverage limit); zero efficiency beyond 2.7 is exactly correct.

extractions.source_summary: Primary: ATLAS Collaboration, "Muon reconstruction performance of the ATLAS detector in proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV", Eur. Phys. J. C 76 (2016) 292, DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-016-4120-y, arXiv:1603.05598 (3.2 fb-1, 2015 data). Authoritative collaboration measurement of muon reconstruction+ID efficiency for the Medium working point (the ATLAS default). Key results used: Abstract + Sec.6 ("reconstruction efficiency close to 99% over most of |eta|<2.5 and 5<pT<100 GeV"); Fig.6 ("efficiency stable and slightly above 99% for pT>6 GeV", 0.1<|eta|<2.5, Z->mumu and J/psi->mumu); Fig.4 ((eta,phi) map of Medium-muon efficiency for pT>10 GeV in Z->mumu, all bins 98-100%); Table 1 (ttbar MC prompt-muon efficiency: Medium = 95.5% for 4<pT<20 GeV, 96.1% for 20<pT<100 GeV, |eta|<2.5); Fig.5 + Sec.6.1 (J/psi low-pT measurement, six pT bins spanning only 5-15 GeV). Sec.6.2: region 2.5<|eta|<2.7 ("high-eta") is covered only by ME/MS-extrapolated muons outside ID acceptance; |eta|>2.7 uncovered. Cross-check available: full Run-2 paper EPJC 81 (2021) 578, arXiv:2012.00578 (139 fb-1), consistent ~99% Medium efficiency. NOTE: the lowest pT measured in any ATLAS muon-reco paper is 5 GeV (J/psi); the sub-1-GeV / 0.1-1 GeV regime in the card has NO published measurement.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card splits |eta| at 1.5 (barrel/endcap-like) with values 0.99 (|eta|<=1.5) vs 0.98 (1.5<|eta|<=2.5). The source measures over the full ID acceptance |eta|<2.5 and shows the Medium efficiency is essentially flat at 98-100% across the whole (eta,phi) plane (Fig.4), with no pronounced barrel/endcap step at |eta|=1.5; localized dips exist (e.g. (eta,phi)~(-1.3,1.6) from a misaligned MDT chamber) but are not captured by a 1.5 boundary. So the card's 1.5 eta split is a coarse, physically reasonable but not source-driven binning. Card pT split at 1.0 GeV does NOT match the source: the source's high-pT plateau (~99%) is established for pT>6 GeV (Fig.6) and Table 1 averages over 4<pT<20 GeV (95.5%) and 20<pT<100 GeV (96.1%); the card therefore applies the plateau value from 1 GeV upward, which is optimistic in the 1-5 GeV window. The card's lowest bin (0.1<pT<1.0 GeV) lies entirely below the measured range (>=5 GeV) and has no source.

coefficients.name: eff_pt_below_0p1_all_eta
coefficients.locator: No measurement; ATLAS muon reco never probes pT below 5 GeV (arXiv:1603.05598 Fig.5/Sec.6.1 lowest bin 5-6 GeV).
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: A hard 0% cutoff at pT<=0.1 GeV is a sensible kinematic floor (such soft muons do not reach/trigger the MS and are far below any measurement); no public number contradicts it, so keep as a modelling choice.

coefficients.name: eff_central_lowpt
coefficients.locator: Below measured range; lowest ATLAS bin is 5-6 GeV (arXiv:1603.05598 Fig.5, Sec.6.1). No source covers 0.1-1 GeV.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (extrapolation only)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current value 0.75 but flag as UNSOURCED extrapolation; recommend documenting it as an assumed turn-on, not a measurement. Suggested uncertainty: assign at least +/-0.10 (modelling).
coefficients.rationale: Muons with pT<1 GeV barely penetrate to the MS; a reduced-but-nonzero efficiency is plausible, but no ATLAS measurement reaches this regime, so the exact 0.75 cannot be validated against literature.

coefficients.name: eff_central_highpt
coefficients.locator: Sec.6/Fig.6 ('efficiency stable and slightly above 99% for pT>6 GeV', 0.1<|eta|<2.5); Fig.4 (eta,phi) map central bins 98.3-100.0%; Abstract ('close to 99% over |eta|<2.5 and 5<pT<100 GeV').
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.99 (central, pT>~6 GeV); Fig.4 central bins 0.983-1.000
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: 0.99 matches the measured Medium-WP barrel plateau (~99% for pT>6 GeV). Mild caveat: applying it from pT>1 GeV is slightly optimistic in 1-6 GeV where efficiency is still rising, but acceptable for a fast-sim card.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_lowpt
coefficients.locator: Below measured range; lowest ATLAS bin 5-6 GeV (arXiv:1603.05598 Fig.5). No source covers 0.1-1 GeV in the endcap.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (extrapolation only)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current value 0.70 but flag as UNSOURCED extrapolation (slightly lower than barrel, consistent with reduced forward coverage); suggested modelling uncertainty +/-0.10.
coefficients.rationale: No ATLAS measurement reaches pT<1 GeV; the 0.70 (5 points below the barrel 0.75) is a reasonable but unvalidated assumption.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_highpt
coefficients.locator: Fig.4 (eta,phi) map, endcap bins 98-100%; Sec.6 'in excess of 98%' for Loose/Medium; Abstract 'close to 99% over |eta|<2.5'; Fig.6 (0.1<|eta|<2.5 combined, >99% for pT>6 GeV).
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.98-0.99 (endcap up to |eta|=2.5)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: 0.98 is consistent with (slightly conservative relative to) the measured Medium-WP endcap efficiency of 98-99% for pT>6 GeV within the ID acceptance |eta|<2.5.

coefficients.name: eff_above_2p5_zero
coefficients.locator: Sec.6.2 'For |eta|>2.5 the efficiency is recovered using ME muons ... region 2.5<|eta|<2.7 (high-eta)'; Sec.2 (ID coverage |eta|<2.5, MS up to |eta|=2.7).
coefficients.extracted_value: Combined-muon reco efficiency = 0 for |eta|>2.5 (no ID); only ME/MS-extrapolated muons recover partial acceptance in 2.5<|eta|<2.7; nothing beyond 2.7.
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (optionally add a partial-efficiency ME-muon bin for 2.5<|eta|<2.7 if forward muons matter for the analysis, but a hard 0 above 2.5 is defensible since combined-muon ID stops at |eta|=2.5).
coefficients.rationale: Setting efficiency to 0 for |eta|>2.5 matches the ID-limited combined-muon acceptance; the only recovery is the low-statistics ME-muon high-eta region (2.5<|eta|<2.7), which the card conservatively ignores.

extractions.source_summary: ATLAS Collaboration, "Measurement of the photon identification efficiencies with the ATLAS detector using LHC Run 2 data collected in 2015 and 2016", Eur. Phys. J. C 79 (2019) 205, DOI:10.1140/epjc/s10052-019-6650-6, CERN-EP-2018-216, arXiv:1810.05087v2 [hep-ex]. Authoritative collaboration measurement of the Tight photon ID efficiency vs ET in 4 eta bins (|eta|<0.6, 0.6-1.37, 1.52-1.81, 1.81-2.37; crack 1.37-1.52 excluded), separately for converted/unconverted isolated photons, ET = 10 GeV to 1.5 TeV, 36.1-36.7 fb-1 at sqrt(s)=13 TeV. Figures 7 (unconverted) and 8 (converted) give the per-bin efficiency curves; Sec. 5.4 (p.21) and Conclusions (p.35) give summary ranges.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Significant. Card uses a single barrel bin |eta|<=1.5 and a single endcap bin 1.5<|eta|<=2.5. ATLAS uses |eta|<0.6 and 0.6<=|eta|<1.37 for the barrel (boundary 1.37, not 1.5), explicitly EXCLUDES the calorimeter crack 1.37<=|eta|<1.52, and uses 1.52<=|eta|<1.81 and 1.81<=|eta|<2.37 for the endcap (upper edge 2.37, not 2.5). The card's 1.5 boundary straddles the crack region, and the card's coverage to 2.5 exceeds the measured 2.37. Card also has no ET dependence whereas ATLAS efficiency varies strongly with ET (45-60% at 10 GeV up to 95-98% above 100 GeV).

coefficients.name: pt_turnon_threshold
coefficients.current_value: 10.0 GeV (efficiency = 0 for pt<=10, plateau value for pt>10)
coefficients.applicability: all eta; photon pt threshold for nonzero efficiency
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5.4 p.21 (Figures 7 and 8 x-axis); Abstract p.1; Conclusions p.35
coefficients.extracted_value: Measurement starts at ET=10 GeV; efficiency there is only 45-60% (not a full plateau). No sharp step turn-on; efficiency rises smoothly with ET.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: spread 45-60% across eta/conversion at ET=10 GeV
coefficients.proposed_revision: Keep 10 GeV as the lower threshold but note the modeling caveat: a hard step from 0 to full plateau at 10 GeV is unphysical; at 10-25 GeV measured eff is ~45-90%. Consider a graded turn-on (e.g. ~0.5 at 10-15 GeV rising to plateau by ~40 GeV) if low-pt photons matter.
coefficients.rationale: ATLAS measures down to ET=10 GeV with efficiency only 45-60% there; the card's instantaneous jump to the full plateau immediately above 10 GeV overstates efficiency in the 10-40 GeV turn-on region.

coefficients.name: eff_barrel
coefficients.applicability: barrel photons, |eta|<=1.5 (card); compare to ATLAS |eta|<0.6 and 0.6-1.37
coefficients.locator: Figure 7(a,b) (unconverted) and Figure 8(a,b) (converted); summary Sec.5.4 p.21 and Conclusions p.35
coefficients.extracted_value: High-ET plateau (ET>100 GeV) ~95-98%; at ET above 250 GeV 95-99% (unconverted)/88-96% (converted). On intermediate plateau (ET~30-50 GeV) central bins reach roughly 0.90-0.95 (plot-read). At ET=10 GeV only 45-60%.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: total uncertainty (stat+syst) ranges ~5-15% for ET<15 GeV, ~5% for 15-25 GeV, ~1% for 25-40 GeV, <=1% above 100 GeV (p.15, p.18-21); data/MC scale-factor uncertainties 0.5-5%
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: 0.95 is consistent with the measured Tight barrel plateau efficiency at high ET (95-98%) and is a defensible asymptotic value; it is optimistic only in the 10-40 GeV turn-on region, captured separately.

coefficients.name: eff_endcap
coefficients.applicability: endcap photons, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5 (card); compare to ATLAS 1.52-1.81 and 1.81-2.37 (crack 1.37-1.52 excluded; no data above 2.37)
coefficients.locator: Figure 7(c,d) (unconverted) and Figure 8(c,d) (converted); summary Sec.5.4 p.21 and Conclusions p.35
coefficients.extracted_value: High-ET plateau ~95-98% overall; above 250 GeV 95-99% (unconverted)/88-96% (converted), endcap toward the lower end. Intermediate plateau (ET~40 GeV) endcap roughly 0.85-0.92 (plot-read), lower than barrel. At ET=10 GeV 45-60%.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: total uncertainty larger in endcap; ~5% (unconverted) and ~2% (converted) in 1.81<=|eta|<2.37 bin (p.18); 0.5-5% data/MC SF
coefficients.proposed_revision: Keep ~0.85 as a representative endcap plateau value but restrict the bin to 1.52<|eta|<2.37 and exclude the crack 1.37-1.52 (set to ~0); the card's 1.5 lower edge and 2.5 upper edge do not match the measured acceptance. 0.85 is reasonable for converted/low-ET endcap but pessimistic vs the high-ET unconverted plateau ~95%.
coefficients.rationale: 0.85 sits below the measured high-ET endcap plateau (~88-96%, up to ~95-98% above 100 GeV) so it is pessimistic at high ET, while the eta binning (1.5-2.5 vs measured 1.52-2.37 with crack excluded) is mismatched; value is acceptable as an effective average but the binning should be corrected.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_zero
coefficients.locator: Measurement coverage stated in Abstract (p.1) and Sec.2; data extend only to |eta|=2.37
coefficients.extracted_value: ATLAS Tight photon ID is measured only up to |eta|=2.37 (EM calorimeter precision/photon ID acceptance ~2.37). No reconstructed Tight photons beyond ~2.37-2.5.
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Zero efficiency beyond |eta|=2.5 is consistent with the photon ID acceptance ending at ~2.37; the card's cut at 2.5 is slightly looser than the measured 2.37 boundary but the asymptotic 0 is correct.

extractions.source_summary: ATLAS Collaboration, "Reconstruction, Energy Calibration, and Identification of Hadronically Decaying Tau Leptons in the ATLAS Experiment for Run-2 of the LHC", ATL-PHYS-PUB-2015-045, CERN, 2015 (https://cds.cern.ch/record/2064383). This is the exact note the card cites and is the collaboration-endorsed public reference for the Run-2 (sqrt(s)=13 TeV) BDT tau identification working points. The Medium-WP combined reconstruction+identification signal efficiencies are stated explicitly in the text on p.11; jet (QCD) mis-tag is given only as the inverse-background-efficiency ROC curve in Fig. 9 (no tabulated point values), and ID-efficiency systematics for the Medium WP are shown in Fig. 12. An earlier, more detailed peer-reviewed companion is the Run-1 measurement arXiv:1412.7086 (Eur. Phys. J. C 75 (2015) 303); the 2015 PUB note supersedes it for Run-2 numbers.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: The card applies flat efficiencies with no pT or eta dependence (only TauEtaMax=2.5, TauPTMin=1.0 GeV cuts, lines 694-695). The source defines the WP efficiencies as constant-in-pT targets for tau pT >= 20 GeV (Fig.9 caption, p.5) and within |eta|<2.5; the card's TauPTMin=1.0 GeV extends the flat efficiency well below the 20 GeV regime where the source does not certify it (3-prong efficiency in particular drops sharply below ~20 GeV, Fig.3/Fig.10b). Source quotes systematics separately for central |eta|<1.37 and forward 1.52<|eta|<2.47 (Fig.12); card has no eta binning.

coefficients.name: tau_eff_1prong
coefficients.applicability: 1-prong hadronic tau, |eta|<2.5, tau pT>1 GeV (card); source value for pT>=20 GeV
coefficients.locator: p.11 text: 'Signal efficiencies are, respectively, 0.6, 0.55 and 0.45 for the 1-prong Loose, Medium and Tight working points.'; also Fig.10(a)
coefficients.extracted_value: 0.55 (Medium WP, 1-prong); 0.60 (Loose), 0.45 (Tight)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ID-eff systematic ~5-10% relative for pT<100 GeV (Fig.12a,c, Medium WP, |eta|<1.37 and 1.52<|eta|<2.47); reaches larger at high pT (pileup-dominated)
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.55 +/- 0.05 (use Medium-WP value, since card explicitly cites 'medium working point')
coefficients.rationale: Card uses 0.70 for the 1-prong Medium WP, but the cited note states the Medium 1-prong efficiency is 0.55 (and even Loose is only 0.60). 0.70 exceeds every WP in the source, so the card overstates the 1-prong efficiency; revise to 0.55 to match the cited medium WP.

coefficients.name: tau_eff_multiprong
coefficients.applicability: two-or-more-prong (3-prong) hadronic tau, |eta|<2.5, tau pT>1 GeV (card); source value for pT>=20 GeV
coefficients.locator: p.11 text: 'The corresponding 3-prong working points have efficiencies of 0.5, 0.4 and 0.3.' (Loose/Medium/Tight); also Fig.10(b)
coefficients.extracted_value: 0.40 (Medium WP, 3-prong); 0.50 (Loose), 0.30 (Tight)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ID-eff systematic up to ~16% relative for 3-prong barrel decays (p.13 text; Fig.12b), ~5-10% elsewhere
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.40 +/- 0.06 (use Medium-WP 3-prong value)
coefficients.rationale: Card uses 0.60 for multi-prong; the cited medium WP 3-prong efficiency is 0.40 (Loose is 0.50). 0.60 exceeds even the Loose WP, so the card overstates multi-prong efficiency; revise to 0.40.

coefficients.name: tau_mistag_1prong
coefficients.applicability: QCD-jet -> 1-track tau fake rate, |eta|<2.5, tau-candidate pT>1 GeV (card)
coefficients.locator: Fig. 9 (p.12), ROC of inverse background efficiency vs signal efficiency, 1-prong curve, read at signal eff = 0.55 (Medium)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated; plot-read: at signal eff ~0.55 the 1-prong inverse-background efficiency is ~30-50, i.e. mistag ~0.02-0.03
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: unknown (no mis-tag uncertainty quoted; ROC read by eye, +/- factor ~1.5)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.02 is consistent with Fig.9 1-prong ROC at the Medium WP); flag as plot-read, not tabulated
coefficients.rationale: Source gives jet mis-tag only as the Fig.9 ROC (no number). Reading the 1-prong curve at signal eff 0.55 gives 1/eps_bkg ~ 30-50 => mistag ~0.02-0.03, consistent with the card's 0.02. Cannot fully confirm because the value is not tabulated.

coefficients.name: tau_mistag_multiprong
coefficients.applicability: QCD-jet -> 3-track tau fake rate, |eta|<2.5, tau-candidate pT>1 GeV (card)
coefficients.locator: Fig. 9 (p.12), ROC of inverse background efficiency vs signal efficiency, 3-prong curve, read at signal eff = 0.40 (Medium)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated; plot-read: at signal eff ~0.40 the 3-prong inverse-background efficiency is ~few-hundred to ~10^3, i.e. mistag ~0.001-0.005
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.003 (+/- factor ~2) [optional]; the card's 0.01 is a few-times higher (conservative). Acceptable to keep current as a deliberately conservative round number.
coefficients.rationale: Fig.9 3-prong curve at signal eff 0.40 implies 1/eps_bkg of several-hundred to ~1000 => mistag ~0.001-0.005, somewhat below the card's 0.01. Card is mildly conservative (over-estimates the multi-prong fake rate). Value is plot-read, not tabulated, so revision is optional.

extractions.source_summary: Card explicitly cites (line 717) arXiv:1211.4462 = CMS Collaboration, "Identification of b-quark jets with the CMS experiment" (CMS-BTV-12-001), JINST 8 (2013) P04013, 7 TeV, 5.0 fb-1. This is the authoritative, peer-reviewed, collaboration-endorsed Run-1 source. Key locators verified in the PDF: Section 4 (p.6) defines Loose/Medium/Tight operating points with light-parton mistag "close to 10%, 1%, and 0.1% respectively, at an average jet pt of about 80 GeV/c"; Fig.6 (p.10/12) gives the c-jet and light-parton mistag-vs-b-efficiency ROC (jets pt>60 GeV); Fig.7 (p.11/13) gives b-jet efficiency and c/light mistag as a function of jet pt and |eta| for the CSVM (Medium CSV) tagger in QCD multijet and ttbar (pt>30 GeV, |eta|<2.4; udsg curve scaled up x10 in the plot; rightmost bin includes pt>500 GeV). The shape and magnitudes of the three card formulas (b-eff plateau ~0.65-0.72, c-mistag ~0.2, light-mistag ~1% near 80 GeV rising with pt) match the CSVM (Medium) working point of this paper. A more modern alternative is the Run-2 paper arXiv:1712.07158 (JINST 13 (2018) P05011, BTV-16-002, DeepCSV/CSVv2/cMVAv2), whose Medium WP reaches ~68% b-eff at 1% light mistag; the card, however, is parametrized to the Run-1 CSVM numbers it cites.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: The card formulas depend on pt only and have NO eta dependence. The cited source (Fig.7c,d of arXiv:1211.4462) explicitly shows b-eff and mistag as a function of jet |eta| up to 2.4 and reports a mild eta dependence (efficiency falls somewhat toward |eta|~2.4). The card therefore averages over |eta|<2.5 with no binning. Also the source's pt working-point statement is anchored at <pt>~80 GeV/c, whereas the card light-mistag formula gives 0.013 at 80 GeV (vs the source's nominal ~0.01 for Medium), a minor offset within the pt-dependent spread shown in Fig.7.

coefficients.name: light_mistag_const_term (PDG 0)
coefficients.locator: Section 4 (p.6 of PDF): Medium operating point defined at light-parton mistag 'close to ... 1% ... at an average jet pt of about 80 GeV/c'; Fig.7(b),(d) (p.11/13) udsg mistag vs pt for CSVM (udsg curve scaled x10 in plot).
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.01 (1%) light-parton mistag at <pt>~80 GeV/c for CSVM (Medium); plot-read low-pt value somewhat below 1%
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~10-15% relative (data/MC scale-factor and template-fit syst, Section 7); not tabulated per-bin in the public text
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Card gives 0.011 at 30 GeV and 0.013 at 80 GeV, bracketing the source's ~1% Medium-WP light-parton mistag at <pt>~80 GeV/c; the constant term sets the low-pt floor at ~1%. Consistent with CSVM. Add an explicit ~10-15% relative uncertainty when documenting.

coefficients.name: light_mistag_pt_slope (PDG 0)
coefficients.applicability: light-flavour (udsg+gluon) jets, |eta|<2.5; rising with pt; PDG 0
coefficients.locator: Fig.7(b),(d) (p.11/13): udsg-jet misidentification probability rises with jet pt for CSVM (text p.13: 'the b-jet efficiency and the c-jet misidentification probability rise with jet pt'); the light mistag likewise increases toward high pt.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated; plot-read positive slope giving roughly 1% at low pt to ~2-3% by several hundred GeV (consistent with 0.01+3.8e-5*pt -> 0.025 at 400 GeV)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: unknown (per-bin uncertainty not tabulated in public text; overall mistag scale syst O(10-20%))
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: The linear rise (0.0138 at 100 GeV, 0.0252 at 400 GeV) reproduces the increasing light-parton mistag of CSVM seen in Fig.7; magnitude and trend agree. Cannot tighten the slope without digitizing the figure, so retain with a noted uncertainty.

coefficients.name: c_mistag_formula (PDG 4)
coefficients.locator: Fig.6(b) (p.10/12): c-jet mistag vs b-efficiency ROC (pt>60 GeV); Fig.7(b),(d) (p.11/13): c-jet mistag vs jet pt for CSVM. At the Medium WP (b-eff~0.65-0.7) the CSV c-jet mistag is in the ~0.15-0.25 band.
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.2 c-jet mistag at the CSVM operating point (b-eff ~0.65-0.7), pt-dependent ~0.1-0.25 (plot-read from Fig.6b/Fig.7)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: unknown per-bin; charm SF uncertainties taken as ~2x the b SF uncertainty in CMS practice (not stated numerically in this paper's public text)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Card c-mistag (0.168 at 50, 0.209 at 100, 0.152 at 500 GeV) sits squarely in the CSVM c-jet-mistag band of Fig.6b/Fig.7, with the correct rise-then-fall pt shape. Consistent with the Medium CSV WP; uncertainty not extractable from the public figures.

coefficients.name: b_eff_formula (PDG 5)
coefficients.current_value: 0.85*tanh(0.0025*pt)*(25.0/(1+0.063*pt))  (rises ~0.47 at 20 GeV to plateau ~0.72 at 100-200 GeV, falls to ~0.55 at 500 GeV)
coefficients.locator: Section 4 (p.6): Medium WP ~1% light mistag at <pt>~80 GeV; Fig.6 (p.10/12) ROC; Fig.7(b),(d) (p.11/13): b-jet efficiency vs jet pt and |eta| for CSVM, y-axis 0-0.8, b-eff in ~0.6-0.7 range, turning on at low pt and decreasing at very high pt.
