coefficients.extracted_value: CSVM b-jet efficiency ~0.65-0.70 on the plateau (Fig.7b,d), turning on below ~50 GeV and decreasing at high pt; abstract headline 70% b-eff corresponds to 1.5% light mistag (tighter than Medium)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: data/MC scale factor SF_b known to ~few % per bin (Section 7 / Fig. of SF_b); typical CMS Run-1 SF_b uncertainty 2-5%
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Card b-eff (0.55 at 30, 0.69 at 80, plateau ~0.72, falling at high pt) matches the CSVM (Medium CSV) efficiency-vs-pt shape and magnitude in Fig.7(b,d). The associated working point (light mistag ~1% near 80 GeV) is reproduced by the card's light-mistag formula, confirming CSVM. Keep; attach ~2-5% per-bin SF_b uncertainty when documenting, and note the card lacks the mild eta dependence shown in Fig.7c,d.

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Description and performance of track and primary-vertex reconstruction with the CMS tracker", JINST 9 (2014) P10009, arXiv:1405.6569 (the source already cited on line 154 of the card). Authoritative: peer-reviewed CMS tracker performance paper. Relevant content: Sec. 5.2 "Resolution in the track parameters", Fig. 14 (sigma_pt/pt vs eta for muons at pt=1,10,100 GeV) and Fig. 15 (sigma_pt/pt in % vs pt, for single isolated muons in barrel 0-0.9 / transition 0.9-1.4 / endcap 1.4-2.5; bottom-center panel). Abstract: "For isolated muons of pT = 100 GeV emitted at |eta| < 1.4, the resolutions are approximately 2.8% in pT". The Delphes MomentumSmearing module (modules/MomentumSmearing.cc line 117-124) uses the ResolutionFormula output directly as the RELATIVE resolution sigma_pt/pt (LogNormal(pt, res*pt)), so a card 'a' value of 0.06 means a 6% constant term. The card's hard-coded constants (6/10/25% floors, b=1.3-3.1e-3 GeV^-1 slopes) are NOT numerically consistent with Fig. 15: measured 68% pt resolution floors are ~0.8-1% (barrel), ~1.5% (transition), ~2-2.5% (endcap), reaching only ~2.5%/~4.5%/~10% at pt=100 GeV. The card is therefore grossly pessimistic and the "based on arXiv:1405.6569" attribution is not supported by the figures; the card numbers appear to be a hand-tuned parametrization rather than a fit of this paper. Note an eta-binning mismatch (card 0.5/1.5/2.5 vs source 0.9/1.4/2.5).
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Yes. Card eta bins are |eta|<=0.5 / 0.5-1.5 / 1.5-2.5. Source (Fig. 15) bins are barrel 0-0.9 / transition 0.9-1.4 / endcap 1.4-2.5. The card's first bin (<=0.5) lies fully inside the source barrel; the card's middle bin (0.5-1.5) straddles barrel+transition+a sliver of endcap; the card's third bin (1.5-2.5) approximately equals the source endcap (1.4-2.5). Proposed revisions below map: bin1 -> barrel curve, bin2 -> transition curve, bin3 -> endcap curve.

coefficients.name: a_eta0_05_const
coefficients.applicability: charged hadron, |eta| <= 0.5, pt > 0.1 GeV; constant (low-pt, multiple-scattering) term of sigma_pt/pt = sqrt(a^2 + (b*pt)^2)
coefficients.locator: Fig. 15 (bottom-center panel: Resolution in pt/pt [%] vs pt), barrel muon curve (eta 0-0.9), solid=68% interval; Sec. 5.2. Cross-check Fig. 14 bottom-center panel.
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read: floor ~0.8-1.0% (min ~0.8% near pt=2-3 GeV; ~1.0% at pt=1 GeV) => a ~ 0.008-0.010 (fraction)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~0.2% absolute spread on plot read (plot-read uncertainty); 68% vs 90% interval differ by ~factor 1.3
coefficients.rationale: Card 0.06 = 6% constant term; Fig. 15 barrel 68% floor is ~0.8-1.0%, so the card is ~6x too large. Read from the bottom-center pt/pt panel of Fig. 15.

coefficients.name: b_eta0_05_slope
coefficients.applicability: charged hadron, |eta| <= 0.5, pt > 0.1 GeV; pt-proportional (high-pt) term coefficient b in sqrt(a^2 + (b*pt)^2), units GeV^-1
coefficients.locator: Fig. 15 bottom-center panel, barrel curve high-pt rise; Abstract ('~2.8% in pT at pt=100 GeV, |eta|<1.4'); Fig. 14 bottom-center at pt=100 GeV.
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read: sigma_pt/pt(100 GeV, barrel) ~ 2-2.5% => b ~ sqrt(0.025^2 - 0.009^2)/100 ~ 2.3e-4 GeV^-1 (abstract gives ~2.8% for the wider |eta|<1.4 average)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~0.5% absolute at 100 GeV (plot read) => b spread ~ +/-0.5e-4 GeV^-1
coefficients.rationale: Card b=1.3e-3 gives 13% pt-term at 100 GeV (total ~14.3%); Fig. 15 barrel shows ~2.5% at 100 GeV, consistent with abstract's 2.8% for |eta|<1.4. Card slope is ~5-6x too steep.

coefficients.name: a_eta05_15_const
coefficients.applicability: charged hadron, 0.5 < |eta| <= 1.5, pt > 0.1 GeV; constant term a
coefficients.locator: Fig. 15 bottom-center panel, transition muon curve (eta 0.9-1.4), solid=68%; this card bin straddles barrel(0-0.9)+transition(0.9-1.4). Sec. 5.2.
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read: transition floor ~1.5% (min near pt=3 GeV); barrel part of this bin ~1% => effective a ~ 0.012-0.018 (fraction)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~0.3% absolute (plot read) + binning-straddle ambiguity (barrel vs transition)
coefficients.rationale: Card 0.10 = 10% floor; measured transition floor is ~1.5%, so card is ~6-7x too large. Bin straddles source barrel/transition (binning mismatch), value taken near transition curve.

coefficients.name: b_eta05_15_slope
coefficients.applicability: charged hadron, 0.5 < |eta| <= 1.5, pt > 0.1 GeV; pt-term coefficient b, GeV^-1
coefficients.locator: Fig. 15 bottom-center panel, transition curve high-pt rise (eta 0.9-1.4) at pt=100 GeV.
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read: sigma_pt/pt(100 GeV, transition) ~ 4-5% => b ~ sqrt(0.045^2 - 0.015^2)/100 ~ 4.2e-4 GeV^-1
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~0.7% absolute at 100 GeV => b spread ~ +/-0.7e-4 GeV^-1
coefficients.rationale: Card b=1.7e-3 gives 17% pt-term at 100 GeV (total ~19.7%); Fig. 15 transition shows ~4.5% at 100 GeV. Card slope is ~4x too steep.

coefficients.name: a_eta15_25_const
coefficients.applicability: charged hadron, 1.5 < |eta| <= 2.5, pt > 0.1 GeV; constant term a
coefficients.locator: Fig. 15 bottom-center panel, endcap muon curve (eta 1.4-2.5), solid=68%; card bin (1.5-2.5) ~ source endcap (1.4-2.5). Sec. 5.2.
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read: endcap floor ~2-2.5% (min near pt=4-5 GeV; ~3.5% near pt=0.3 GeV) => a ~ 0.020-0.025 (fraction)
coefficients.rationale: Card 0.25 = 25% floor; measured endcap floor is ~2-2.5%, so card is ~10x too large. This card bin matches the source endcap binning well.

coefficients.name: b_eta15_25_slope
coefficients.applicability: charged hadron, 1.5 < |eta| <= 2.5, pt > 0.1 GeV; pt-term coefficient b, GeV^-1
coefficients.locator: Fig. 15 bottom-center panel, endcap curve high-pt rise (eta 1.4-2.5) at pt=100 GeV.
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read: sigma_pt/pt(100 GeV, endcap) ~ 9-10% => b ~ sqrt(0.10^2 - 0.023^2)/100 ~ 9.7e-4 GeV^-1
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~1% absolute at 100 GeV => b spread ~ +/-1e-4 GeV^-1
coefficients.rationale: Card b=3.1e-3 gives 31% pt-term at 100 GeV (total ~39.8%); Fig. 15 endcap shows ~10% at 100 GeV. Card slope is ~3x too steep. This is the closest-matching bin but still pessimistic by ~3-4x.

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Description and performance of track and primary-vertex reconstruction with the CMS tracker", JINST 9 (2014) P10009, arXiv:1405.6569. Authoritative collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed measurement of CMS tracking performance. Relevant content: Figure 8 (middle) gives single, isolated charged-pion (charged-hadron) track-reconstruction efficiency vs eta (for pT=1,10,100 GeV) and vs pT (barrel/transition/endcap regions), high-purity tracks. Figure 10 (top) gives the charged-particle tracking efficiency in simulated ttbar events (with pileup), which closely resembles the isolated-pion result. Text states: efficiency approximately constant for 1<pT<80 GeV; at small pT efficiency drops quickly (pion-nucleus cross-section rises below ~0.7 GeV); up to 20% of pions not reconstructed depending on eta. Quoted averages for pT>0.9 GeV: 94% for |eta|<0.9 and 85% for 0.9<|eta|<2.5. The Delphes card uses a coarser 2-region eta binning (|eta|<=1.5 ; 1.5<|eta|<=2.5) and 2-region pT binning (0.1-1.0 ; >1.0 GeV), so it is a step-function approximation of the smooth Fig.8/Fig.10 curves.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Yes. Card eta bins are |eta|<=1.5 and 1.5<|eta|<=2.5; the source quotes averages in |eta|<0.9 (94%) and 0.9<|eta|<2.5 (85%), and Fig.8/Fig.10 are continuous in eta. The card's central bin (|eta|<=1.5) spans both the source's high-efficiency barrel (|eta|<0.9, ~94%) and the lower-efficiency 0.9-1.5 transition region; the card's forward bin (1.5-2.5) corresponds to part of the source's 0.9<|eta|<2.5 (~85%) average. Card pT bins (0.1-1.0, >1.0 GeV) are a 2-step approximation of the continuous low-pT turn-on (drop below ~0.7 GeV) shown in Fig.8/Fig.10 (right); the source plateau begins near pT~1 GeV, consistent with the card's threshold.

coefficients.name: eff_pt_threshold_zero
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5.4 / Conclusions: 'finding charged particles with pT as low as 0.1 GeV'; Fig. 8 (middle, right) and Fig. 10 (top-right) efficiency vs pT going to ~0 at the low-pT edge
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0 (no reconstruction below pT ~ 0.1 GeV; tracking acceptance floor stated as pT as low as 0.1 GeV)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Source states tracking reaches pT as low as 0.1 GeV and Fig.8/Fig.10 efficiency-vs-pT curves fall toward zero at this edge; card's hard 0 below 0.1 GeV is a reasonable acceptance cut, consistent.

coefficients.name: eff_central_lowpt
coefficients.locator: Fig. 8 (middle, right) single-pion efficiency vs pT, barrel region; Fig. 10 (top-right) ttbar charged-particle efficiency vs pT; text Sec. 5.1.2 'at small pT, the efficiency decreases quickly ... pion-nucleus cross section increases rapidly below 0.7 GeV'
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read ~0.5-0.85 rising across 0.1->1.0 GeV in barrel (steep turn-on; below ~0.7 GeV efficiency drops well below the ~0.9 plateau)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~10% (plot-read spread over the pT bin; no tabulated value)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.70 +/- 0.10); a single step value of 0.70 is a defensible bin-average of the steep 0.1-1.0 GeV turn-on in the barrel, but it is a coarse approximation of a strongly pT-dependent curve
coefficients.rationale: Source has no tabulated single number for this bin; Fig.8/Fig.10 show a steep low-pT turn-on in the barrel that averages to roughly 0.7 over 0.1-1.0 GeV, so 0.70 is a plausible bin-average, assigned ~10% plot-read uncertainty.

coefficients.name: eff_central_highpt
coefficients.locator: Abstract/Conclusions: avg track-reco efficiency 94% for |eta|<0.9, pT>0.9 GeV; Fig. 8 (middle) and Fig. 10 (top) high-purity efficiency vs eta (plateau ~0.9-0.95 in barrel); text 'approximately constant for 1<pT<80 GeV'
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.94 (barrel |eta|<0.9 average); decreasing toward ~0.85-0.90 in the 0.9-1.5 transition part of the card bin
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~2-3% (read from quoted 94% and Fig.8/Fig.10 plateau spread; no explicit error bar tabulated)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current, but note 0.95 is slightly optimistic vs the quoted 94% (|eta|<0.9) and overstates the lower-efficiency 0.9<|eta|<1.5 portion folded into the card's |eta|<=1.5 bin; a value of ~0.93 +/- 0.02 would better match the bin-averaged source
coefficients.rationale: Source quotes 94% for |eta|<0.9 and the efficiency drops in the 0.9-1.5 transition region included in the card's central bin, so the bin-averaged efficiency is slightly below 0.95; 0.95 is within ~1-2% and broadly consistent but marginally optimistic.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_lowpt
coefficients.locator: Fig. 8 (middle, right) single-pion efficiency vs pT, endcap region; Fig. 10 (top-right); text 'depending on eta, up to 20% of pions are not reconstructed ... most significant for pT <~ 700 MeV'
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read ~0.4-0.8 rising across 0.1->1.0 GeV in endcap (turn-on lower than barrel due to larger forward material; steep below ~0.7 GeV)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~10% (plot-read spread over the pT bin; no tabulated value)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.60 +/- 0.10); a single step value of 0.60 is a defensible bin-average of the endcap low-pT turn-on, lower than the barrel as expected, but coarse
coefficients.rationale: No tabulated number; Fig.8/Fig.10 endcap curves show a lower, steep low-pT turn-on (more material, larger nuclear-interaction losses forward) averaging to roughly 0.6 over 0.1-1.0 GeV, so 0.60 is a plausible bin-average with ~10% plot-read uncertainty.

coefficients.name: eff_forward_highpt
coefficients.locator: Abstract/Conclusions: avg track-reco efficiency 85% for 0.9<|eta|<2.5, pT>0.9 GeV; Fig. 8 (middle) and Fig. 10 (top) efficiency vs eta (drops toward ~0.8-0.85 at high |eta|)
coefficients.extracted_value: ~0.85 (quoted average for 0.9<|eta|<2.5; Fig.8/Fig.10 show ~0.8-0.85 in the forward region)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~3% (read from quoted 85% and Fig.8/Fig.10 spread; no explicit tabulated error)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.85 +/- 0.03)
coefficients.rationale: Source explicitly quotes 85% average for 0.9<|eta|<2.5 at pT>0.9 GeV; card's forward high-pT value of 0.85 matches this directly (card bin 1.5-2.5 is a subset of the source's 0.9-2.5 average).

coefficients.name: eff_eta_outside_acceptance
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5 and Conclusions: 'tracking algorithms reconstruct tracks over the full pseudorapidity range of the tracker |eta| < 2.5'; single particles generated flat in |eta| < 2.5 acceptance
coefficients.extracted_value: 0 (tracker acceptance ends at |eta| = 2.5)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: Source repeatedly states the tracker acceptance is |eta|<2.5; zero efficiency beyond 2.5 is exactly correct for the Run-1 tracker geometry described.

extractions.source_summary: Primary energy-shape source: CMS Collaboration, "Energy calibration and resolution of the CMS electromagnetic calorimeter in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV", CMS-EGM-11-001, CERN-PH-EP/2013-097, arXiv:1306.2016, published JINST 8 (2013) P09009, doi:10.1088/1748-0221/8/09/P09009 (collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed). Its Eq. (1) gives the test-beam ECAL barrel resolution sigma_E/E = 2.8%/sqrt(E) (+) 12%/E (+) 0.3% (stochastic (+) noise (+) constant; 3x3 crystal matrix; ref [20] = CMS NIM/JINST test-beam paper). The card cites BOTH 1306.2016 (eta shape) and 1502.02701 (energy shape) on lines 301-302. NOTE: arXiv:1502.02701 is "Performance of electron reconstruction and selection with the CMS detector at sqrt(s)=8 TeV" and reports electron momentum/energy resolution of 1.7-4.5%, not a closed S/N/C ECAL form. CRITICAL FINDING: the energy-shape coefficients actually hard-coded in the card (S=11%, N=0.40 GeV, C=0.8%) do NOT match Eq.(1) of 1306.2016 (S=2.8%, N=0.12 GeV, C=0.3%); they are the historical degraded "default Delphes" numbers. The eta prefactors (1+0.64*eta^2) and (2.16+5.6*(|eta|-2)^2) are Delphes-internal ad-hoc fits to the qualitative eta-degradation described in 1306.2016 Sec. 5 (lines 1525-1529: resolution degrades with material up to |eta|~2.0); no such algebraic prefactor or coefficients (0.64, 2.16, 5.6) appears in the paper. The forward region (|eta|>2.5: C=0.107, N=2.08) is outside the |eta|<2.5 coverage of 1306.2016 and has no cited source.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card eta binning for the resolution formula: barrel |eta|<=1.5, transition/endcap 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, forward 2.5<|eta|<=5.0. Source 1306.2016 covers only |eta|<2.5 (electron/photon acceptance limit, EB |eta|<1.48, EE up to 2.5), and reports MEAN resolutions per region (barrel dielectron mass resolution 1.65%, endcap 2.59%; photon mean energy resolution 2.5% barrel / 4.7% endcap) rather than a binned S/N/C table or a polynomial eta prefactor. The card's smooth prefactors (1+0.64 eta^2) and (2.16+5.6(|eta|-2)^2) have no counterpart binning in the source. The 2.5<|eta|<5.0 (HF/forward) region is entirely outside the source coverage.

coefficients.name: barrel_prefactor_const
coefficients.locator: arXiv:1306.2016 (JINST 8 (2013) P09009) Eq.(1) normalisation at eta=0; qualitative eta-dependence in Sec.5 (paper text lines ~1525-1529)
coefficients.extracted_value: 1 (prefactor normalised to 1 at eta=0 so the core equals the central resolution)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: The leading '1' simply normalises the barrel prefactor to unity at eta=0, consistent with the source quoting a central resolution; not an independently measured coefficient.

coefficients.name: barrel_prefactor_eta2_coeff
coefficients.applicability: ECAL barrel, |eta| <= 1.5; degradation of resolution toward barrel edge
coefficients.locator: Not in arXiv:1306.2016. Paper Sec.5 (lines ~1525-1529) only states resolution degrades with material/near module boundaries; no algebraic (1+0.64 eta^2) form or value 0.64 is given. Not present in arXiv:1502.02701.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (no closed-form eta prefactor in either cited paper)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current value 0.64 but FLAG as a Delphes-internal ad-hoc parametrisation; cite as such (no measured source). If a measured eta dependence is required, derive from 1306.2016 Fig.9/Sec.5 dielectron resolution (barrel 1.65%) -- but the paper provides no 0.64 coefficient.
coefficients.rationale: The eta^2 coefficient 0.64 is a Delphes tuning constant approximating the qualitative barrel degradation described in 1306.2016; the cited papers contain no value for it, so it cannot be confirmed.

coefficients.name: endcap_prefactor_const
coefficients.locator: Not in arXiv:1306.2016 (which gives only mean endcap resolutions, e.g. dielectron 2.59%, photon 4.7%; Sec.5 lines ~1527-1529). No (2.16+5.6(|eta|-2)^2) form or value 2.16 appears. Not in 1502.02701.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current value 2.16 but FLAG as Delphes ad-hoc; no measured source. Cross-check: at |eta|=2, prefactor=2.16, multiplying the ~ (3-5)%-level core gives the few-% endcap resolution mentioned qualitatively, but 2.16 itself is not a measured number.
coefficients.rationale: Endcap prefactor constant 2.16 is a Delphes fit constant with no value in the cited (or any located) CMS paper.

coefficients.name: endcap_prefactor_eta2_coeff
coefficients.locator: Not in arXiv:1306.2016 or arXiv:1502.02701; no such polynomial coefficient is tabulated. 1306.2016 Sec.5 only notes eta dependence up to |eta|~2.0 correlated with upstream material.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current value 5.6 but FLAG as Delphes ad-hoc parametrisation (no measured source).
coefficients.rationale: 5.6 is a Delphes tuning coefficient with no counterpart in the cited papers.

coefficients.name: endcap_prefactor_eta_offset
coefficients.applicability: ECAL transition/endcap, 1.5 < |eta| <= 2.5; pivot pseudorapidity of the parabola
coefficients.locator: Not in arXiv:1306.2016/1502.02701; a pivot at |eta|=2 is plausibly motivated by 1306.2016 Sec.5 (eta dependence saturating near |eta|~2.0, lines ~1528) but no formula fixes the value 2.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (qualitative |eta|~2.0 turnover mentioned in 1306.2016 Sec.5)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current value 2 but FLAG as ad-hoc; loosely consistent with the |eta|~2.0 saturation noted in 1306.2016 Sec.5 but not a quoted parameter.
coefficients.rationale: The eta=2 pivot of the endcap parabola is a Delphes choice; the paper mentions |eta|~2.0 only qualitatively, providing no fitted value.

coefficients.name: energy_shape_constant_C_barrel_endcap
coefficients.current_value: 0.008 (i.e. C = 0.8%; energy^2*0.008^2 term, shared by barrel and endcap)
coefficients.locator: arXiv:1306.2016 Eq.(1), p.4-5 (paper text lines 157-162): sigma/E = 2.8%/sqrt(E) (+) 12%/E (+) 0.3% -> constant term C = 0.3% = 0.003
coefficients.extracted_value: C = 0.3% = 0.003 (test-beam, 3x3 matrix)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: design target <0.3%; in-situ additional spread kept within 0.4% (1306.2016 lines 174-178)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Source-faithful value is C=0.003 (0.3%). Card uses 0.008 (0.8%), ~2.7x larger (pessimistic). If matching 1306.2016 Eq.(1): propose C=0.003 +/- ~0.001. If the intent is a realistic in-situ/pileup-degraded supercluster constant term, the ~0.5-0.8% range is defensible but is NOT the cited Eq.(1) value and should carry a different citation/justification.
coefficients.rationale: Eq.(1) test-beam constant term is 0.3%; card hard-codes 0.8%, i.e. degraded relative to the cited source. Either revise to 0.003 to match the cited paper or re-justify 0.008 with an in-situ/pileup source (none cited).

coefficients.name: energy_shape_stochastic_S_barrel_endcap
coefficients.current_value: 0.11 (i.e. S = 11%; energy*0.11^2 term, shared barrel and endcap)
coefficients.extracted_value: S = 2.8% = 0.028 (test-beam, 3x3 matrix); paper notes magnet field and upstream material worsen S in situ (lines 182-184)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: unknown (single mean value quoted in Eq.(1))
coefficients.proposed_revision: Source-faithful value is S=0.028 (2.8%). Card uses 0.11 (11%), ~4x larger. Propose S=0.028 to match cited 1306.2016 Eq.(1) if a test-beam-faithful card is intended; otherwise the 11% reflects in-situ supercluster/PF-photon degradation under material+pileup which is plausible but uncited -- flag and source separately.
coefficients.rationale: Eq.(1) gives S=2.8%; card hard-codes 11%, far more pessimistic. The card's value is the legacy Delphes degraded number, not the cited paper's measurement.

coefficients.name: energy_shape_noise_N_barrel_endcap
coefficients.current_value: 0.40 (i.e. N = 0.40 GeV; +0.40^2 term, shared barrel and endcap)
coefficients.locator: arXiv:1306.2016 Eq.(1) and surrounding text (lines 157-168): noise term = 12%/E(GeV); '12% at 1 GeV ~ single-channel 40 MeV, giving 120 MeV in a 3x3 matrix' -> N = 0.12 GeV
coefficients.extracted_value: N = 12%/E i.e. N = 0.12 GeV (= 120 MeV over 3x3 matrix at 2010-2011 pileup; lines 167-168)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~40 MeV single-channel; pileup contribution negligible in 2010-2011 (lines 184-186)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Source-faithful value is N=0.12 GeV. Card uses 0.40 GeV, ~3.3x larger. Propose N=0.12 GeV to match cited Eq.(1); the 0.40 GeV is plausibly a high-pileup/wider-supercluster degraded value but is uncited -- flag and source separately.
coefficients.rationale: Eq.(1) noise term corresponds to 0.12 GeV; card hard-codes 0.40 GeV, more pessimistic (consistent with a high-pileup scenario but not with the cited 2010-2011 measurement).

coefficients.name: forward_HF_constant_C
coefficients.locator: Outside coverage of arXiv:1306.2016 (|eta|<2.5). No value located in the cited papers; no forward/HF EM resolution source is cited in the card.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (region not covered by cited source)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current 0.107 but FLAG: no source. Needs a CMS HF / forward-calorimeter EM resolution reference (e.g. CMS HF test-beam or HCAL TDR); currently unsourced.
coefficients.rationale: Forward-region coefficient 0.107 lies beyond the |eta|<2.5 acceptance of the cited papers and has no located public source.

coefficients.name: forward_HF_stochastic_N
coefficients.locator: Outside coverage of arXiv:1306.2016 (|eta|<2.5); no value in cited papers; no HF EM-resolution source cited in card.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (region not covered by cited source)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current 2.08 but FLAG: no source. Needs a CMS HF forward-calorimeter EM resolution reference; currently unsourced.
coefficients.rationale: Forward-region coefficient 2.08 is beyond the cited papers' acceptance and has no located public source.

extractions.source_summary: Primary authoritative source: CMS Collaboration, "Performance of electron reconstruction and selection with the CMS detector in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 8 TeV", JINST 10 (2015) P06005, doi:10.1088/1748-0221/10/06/P06005, arXiv:1502.02701 (CMS-EGM-13-001). It is the collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed reference for GSF electron reconstruction efficiency and the cut-based ID working points. Verified verbatim from the paper text: "The reconstruction efficiency in the data ranges from 88% to 98% in the barrel and from 90% to 96% in the endcaps in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV"; and "Three working points were originally designed to have average efficiencies of about 90, 80, and 70% for electrons from Z -> e+e- events, and were optimized separately for electrons in the ECAL barrel and endcaps." A modern complementary source is CMS, "Electron and photon reconstruction and identification with the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC", JINST 16 (2021) P05014, arXiv:2012.06888 (13 TeV). The Delphes formula multiplies reco x ID into a single per-electron efficiency; no reference is currently cited in the card (confirmed in audit_CMS.md line 21). NOTE: the card combines RECO and ID; the paper reports them separately, so card numbers must be compared against reco(eta,pt) x ID_WP.

coefficients.name: eff_pt_threshold_lowpt
coefficients.locator: Sec. 6 (Efficiency measurements); efficiency-vs-pT figures (Fig. 18-19) start the quoted reco-efficiency range at pT = 10 GeV ('in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV').
coefficients.extracted_value: Not a measured coefficient; the paper does not quote efficiencies below 10 GeV and reco efficiency is rising/low there. The 0.00 is a modelling acceptance/turn-on cut, not a measured value.
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: A hard pT>10 GeV turn-on is a standard Delphes analysis-acceptance choice consistent with the paper only quoting efficiencies for pT>=10 GeV; no source value exists below threshold, so keep as a modelling cut.

coefficients.name: eff_barrel_highpt
coefficients.applicability: barrel, |eta| <= 1.5, pt > 10 GeV (combined reco x ID)
coefficients.locator: Sec. 6 text: 'reconstruction efficiency in the data ranges from 88% to 98% in the barrel ... in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV' (Fig. 18, efficiency vs pT, barrel); Sec. 5 text: working points 'about 90, 80, and 70%' (Fig. 17, barrel).
coefficients.extracted_value: Reco barrel ~0.88-0.98 (rising with pT, plateau ~0.97-0.98 above ~30 GeV); folding a loose ID WP (~0.90) gives combined ~0.85-0.90 at plateau; bare reco alone is ~0.95-0.98.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~+/-0.5% on plateau reco (data/MC scale factors at percent level); ID WP spread ~90/80/70%
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.90 +/- 0.03 (if reco x loose-ID is intended); keep 0.95 only if the card represents reco x very-loose/veto selection. Recommend documenting as reco(>=0.97 plateau) x ID_loose(~0.90).
coefficients.rationale: 0.95 matches bare GSF reco plateau in the barrel, but the Delphes value nominally folds in identification; once a realistic loose/medium ID WP (~90/80%) is included the combined barrel efficiency drops to ~0.85-0.90, so 0.95 is optimistic for a reco+ID number.

coefficients.name: eff_endcap_highpt
coefficients.applicability: endcap, 1.5 < |eta| <= 2.5, pt > 10 GeV (combined reco x ID)
coefficients.locator: Sec. 6 text: 'reconstruction efficiency ... from 90% to 96% in the endcaps in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV' (Fig. 18-19, endcap); Sec. 5 working points 'about 90, 80, 70%' optimized separately for the ECAL endcaps (Fig. 17b).
coefficients.extracted_value: Reco endcap ~0.90-0.96 (plateau ~0.95-0.96 at high pT); folding loose ID WP (~0.84-0.90, endcap WP slightly lower than barrel per Fig. 17b ~84%) gives combined ~0.80-0.86.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~+/-0.8% on plateau reco; ID WP endcap ~84% (loose-equiv quoted in text 'about 90% and 84%')
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.85), optionally 0.85 +/- 0.05
coefficients.rationale: Combined endcap reco (~0.95) x loose ID (~0.84-0.90) ~ 0.80-0.86 brackets the card's 0.85; the card value is a reasonable central estimate, so keep with an added ~+/-0.05 uncertainty.

coefficients.name: eff_acceptance_cutoff
coefficients.locator: Sec. 2-3 (detector/reconstruction): GSF electron reconstruction is restricted to the ECAL/tracker fiducial region |eta| < 2.5; no efficiency is measured beyond |eta|=2.5.
coefficients.extracted_value: 0 (outside tracker/ECAL electron acceptance, |eta| < 2.5)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: |eta|>2.5 is outside the CMS GSF-electron fiducial acceptance, so zero efficiency is correct and matches the paper's |eta|<2.5 coverage.

extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card uses a single barrel/endcap split at |eta|=1.5; the CMS source uses the ECAL barrel/endcap transition at |eta|=1.479 (gap region 1.444 < |eta| < 1.566 excluded in many measurements). Card outer edge |eta|=2.5 matches the CMS electron tracker/ECAL acceptance. Card has only two eta bins and a flat-in-pT plateau above 10 GeV, whereas the source efficiency is strongly pT-dependent (reco 88->98% barrel, 90->96% endcap across 10-100 GeV) and ID adds further pT dependence; the flat card values approximate the high-pT plateau and do not capture the 10-30 GeV turn-on. No fine eta binning (e.g. 0-0.8, 0.8-1.444, 1.566-2.0, 2.0-2.5) used in the source figures is reflected in the card.

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Performance of electron reconstruction and selection with the CMS detector in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=8 TeV", EPJC 75 (2015) 212, arXiv:1502.02701 (published JINST/EPJC, collaboration-endorsed). This is the paper cited in the card (line 171). Authoritative measured electron momentum/energy resolution. Key results relevant to the Delphes sqrt(a^2+(b*pt)^2) relative-resolution form: (i) ABSTRACT + Sec 4.8.4 (lines 32-34, 1472-1474): "The momentum resolution for electrons produced in Z boson decays ranges from 1.7 to 4.5%, depending on electron pseudorapidity and energy loss through bremsstrahlung" -- the 1.6/1.7% end is barrel golden (well-measured) electrons, the 4.1/4.5% end is endcap showering electrons. (ii) Sec 4.8.2 (lines 1356-1357): the additional constant term in the energy resolution (delta-sigma_e) ranges from (0.92 +/- 0.03)% for |eta|<1, R9>=0.94 to (2.90 +/- 0.03)% for |eta|>2, R9<0.94. The electron resolution is ECAL/SC-energy dominated (combined ESC+p), so the relative resolution is roughly FLAT vs pt at Z energies, NOT growing linearly with pt. The paper does NOT tabulate an explicit S/N/C ECAL parametrization (it defers to Ref [4] for ECAL calibration). NOTE: the card's b coefficients (1.3e-3,1.7e-3,3.1e-3 /GeV) are byte-for-byte identical to the tracker/charged-hadron block (lines 155-157), i.e. they are TRACKER momentum-resolution slopes, physically inappropriate for an ECAL-dominated electron resolution.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card uses |eta|<=0.5 / 0.5-1.5 / 1.5-2.5. CMS 1502.02701 reports by ECAL geometry (barrel EB |eta|<1.479, endcap EE 1.479-2.5) and by electron class (golden/showering) and by R9 categories (|eta|<1, 1-1.479, 1.479-2, >2), NOT by the card's 0.5/1.5 boundaries. The card's 0.5 and 1.5 boundaries are a Delphes convention and do not correspond to any boundary in the source; in particular the EB/EE transition is at 1.479, close to the card's 1.5 boundary, so the card's 3rd bin (1.5-2.5) maps roughly to the CMS endcap and the first two bins (0-1.5) both fall in the CMS barrel.

coefficients.name: a_eta0_05 (constant term, |eta|<=0.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, |eta|<=0.5, pt>0.1 GeV; constant (pt-independent) term of sigma_pt/pt = sqrt(a^2+(b*pt)^2)
coefficients.locator: Sec 4.8.2 lines 1356-1357 (constant term 0.92% for |eta|<1, R9>=0.94); Abstract / Sec 4.8.4 lines 32-34,1472-1474 (effective momentum resolution 1.7% barrel golden)
coefficients.extracted_value: constant term ~0.92% (0.0092); barrel golden effective momentum resolution ~1.7% (0.017)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: +/-0.03% on the 0.92% constant term; data/sim agreement <10% on effective resolution (Sec 4.8.4 line 1501)
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.017 +/- 0.002 (use measured barrel effective momentum resolution ~1.7%); acceptable alternative 0.020. Rationale: card 3% is ~2x the CMS-measured ~1.5-1.7% barrel resolution.
coefficients.rationale: Extracted from the abstract's 1.7% lower edge (barrel, low-brem) and the 0.92% constant term in Sec 4.8.2. The card's a=0.03 (3%) overstates the constant/floor by roughly a factor of two for the central barrel; CMS measures ~1.5-1.7%.

coefficients.name: b_eta0_05 (pt slope, |eta|<=0.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, |eta|<=0.5, pt>0.1 GeV; coefficient of the pt-proportional term (b*pt) in sigma_pt/pt
coefficients.locator: No tabulated pt-slope for electrons in 1502.02701; value is identical to the tracker charged-hadron block (delphes_card_CMS.tcl line 155) which traces to arXiv:1405.6569
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (electron resolution is ECAL-dominated and roughly flat vs pt at Z energies; see Fig 12a, Sec 4.8.3)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Re-derive or set ~0 / small. Rationale: 1.3e-3/GeV is a tracker-momentum slope copied from the charged-hadron block; for an ECAL-dominated electron it makes resolution grow to ~6% at pt=45 GeV (sqrt(0.03^2+(45*1.3e-3)^2)=0.066), contradicting the measured ~1.7-2% at Z energies. A near-constant term (small b) matches CMS Fig 12a.
coefficients.rationale: The b coefficient is byte-identical to the tracker charged-hadron card and represents a tracker momentum slope, not the ECAL-dominated electron behavior; it makes the electron resolution rise with pt whereas CMS shows it is roughly flat/improving with energy. No electron-specific source supports this value.

coefficients.name: a_eta05_15 (constant term, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5)
coefficients.locator: Sec 4.8.2 lines 1356-1357 (constant term 0.92% to 2.90% across categories; |eta|~1-1.479 still ECAL barrel); Abstract lines 32-34 (1.7-4.5% range)
coefficients.extracted_value: constant term roughly 1-2% in the outer barrel (between the 0.92% |eta|<1 and the 2.90% |eta|>2 endpoints); effective momentum resolution ~2-3% for medium-pt outer-barrel electrons (Sec 4.8.1 line 1279 'effective resolution in the range of 2-3% for medium-pT')
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: +/-0.03% on quoted constant-term endpoints; data/sim <10% on effective resolution
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.025 +/- 0.005 (outer-barrel effective resolution ~2-3%). Rationale: card 5% is somewhat high vs CMS ~2-3% but less severely off than the central-barrel and endcap bins.
coefficients.rationale: Extracted from the 2-3% medium-pt effective resolution (Sec 4.8.1) and the constant-term range spanning 0.92-2.90% (Sec 4.8.2); the outer barrel sits near the low end (~1-2%), so the card's 5% is mildly pessimistic.

coefficients.name: b_eta05_15 (pt slope, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, 0.5<|eta|<=1.5, pt>0.1 GeV; pt-proportional term coefficient
coefficients.locator: No tabulated electron pt-slope in 1502.02701; value identical to tracker charged-hadron block (line 156, arXiv:1405.6569)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (ECAL-dominated, roughly flat vs pt)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Re-derive or set small; same issue as b_eta0_05. Rationale: copied tracker slope, not electron-appropriate.
coefficients.rationale: Identical to the tracker charged-hadron slope; physically inappropriate for ECAL-dominated electron resolution which CMS shows is roughly flat with energy. No electron source supports it.

coefficients.name: a_eta15_25 (constant term, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5 (ECAL endcap, EE >1.479), pt>0.1 GeV; constant term
coefficients.locator: Sec 4.8.2 lines 1356-1357 (constant term up to (2.90 +/- 0.03)% for |eta|>2, R9<0.94); Abstract / Sec 4.8.4 lines 32-34,1472-1474 (upper edge 4.1-4.5% = endcap showering electrons)
coefficients.extracted_value: constant term up to 2.90% (0.029); worst-case (endcap showering) effective momentum resolution ~4.1-4.5% (0.041-0.045)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: +/-0.03% on the 2.90% constant term; effective resolution data/sim agreement <10%
coefficients.proposed_revision: 0.045 +/- 0.005 (use the 4.5% worst-case endcap showering effective resolution as a conservative floor; ~0.029 if using the constant term alone). Rationale: card 15% is ~3-5x the CMS-measured maximum of ~4.5%.
coefficients.rationale: CMS's largest quoted electron resolution is 4.5% (endcap, showering, Abstract) with a constant term up to 2.90% (Sec 4.8.2). The card's a=0.15 (15%) is a factor of ~3-5 larger than any measured value, strongly pessimistic.

coefficients.name: b_eta15_25 (pt slope, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5)
coefficients.applicability: electron, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>0.1 GeV; pt-proportional term coefficient
coefficients.locator: No tabulated electron pt-slope in 1502.02701; value identical to tracker charged-hadron block (line 157, arXiv:1405.6569)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (ECAL-dominated, roughly flat vs pt)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Re-derive or set small; same tracker-copy issue. Rationale: at pt=45 GeV this term alone gives 45*3.1e-3=0.14, dominating and producing ~20% total, far above CMS ~4.5%.
coefficients.rationale: Identical to the tracker charged-hadron endcap slope; for ECAL-dominated electrons it produces a resolution that rises steeply with pt (~20% at pt=45 GeV in this bin), contradicting CMS's flat ~4.5% maximum. No electron source supports it.

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Performance of electron reconstruction and selection with the CMS detector in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=8 TeV", JINST 10 (2015) P06005, arXiv:1502.02701. Authoritative collaboration-endorsed measurement of GSF-electron reconstruction efficiency (track matched to supercluster) via tag-and-probe on Z->ee. Relevant content: Section 6.1 "Reconstruction efficiency" (p.36) and Figure 23 (reco efficiency vs ESC_T for a) |eta|<0.8 and b) 1.57<|eta|<2). Key statements: "The SC reconstruction efficiency for ESC_T > 5 GeV is close to 100%"; "The efficiencies are found to be >85% for ESC_T > 10 GeV, for all eta"; systematic-dominated uncertainty "a few percent for ESC_T < 20 GeV and decreasing to <1% as ESC_T increases". The card's electron track-momentum-resolution block already cites this same paper (line 171), so it is the intended reference. NOTE: the paper measures down only to ESC_T ~5-10 GeV; it provides NO source for the card's sub-GeV (0.1-1 GeV) bins, and its eta binning does not match the card's 0/1.5/2.5 boundaries.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Yes. Card uses |eta|<=1.5 (barrel) and 1.5<|eta|<=2.5 (endcap), zero above 2.5. The CMS source (Fig. 23) reports only two representative eta slices: |eta|<0.8 (deep barrel) and 1.57<|eta|<2 (endcap, NOT extending to the card's 2.5 edge, and not covering the 0.8-1.444 barrel nor the 1.444-1.566 ECAL crack). So neither card eta bin maps cleanly onto a measured bin; the endcap upper edge (2.0 measured vs 2.5 in card) and the ECAL crack region (where efficiency drops) are unrepresented in the card's step function.

coefficients.name: eff_lowpt_floor (pt<=0.1 GeV)
coefficients.locator: n/a - below measured range; paper covers ESC_T > ~5 GeV (Sec 6.1, p.36)
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: A hard 0 below 0.1 GeV is a sensible kinematic floor (electrons of 0.1 GeV pT do not produce reconstructable GSF tracks/SCs), but 1502.02701 does not measure this region, so no published value confirms it. Keep as a conventional floor.

coefficients.name: eff_barrel_lowpt (|eta|<=1.5, 0.1<pt<=1.0)
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.1 / Fig.23a only down to ESC_T ~5-10 GeV; this sub-GeV bin is outside measured range
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (paper has no measurement below ~5 GeV)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.73), but flag as unsourced; document as an extrapolation/assumption rather than a measured value
coefficients.rationale: The card's 0.1-1.0 GeV barrel bin lies entirely below the CMS measured range (ESC_T > ~5 GeV, robust only >10 GeV). 1502.02701 cannot confirm or refute 0.73; it is an unmeasured low-pT assumption.

coefficients.name: eff_barrel_midpt (|eta|<=1.5, 1.0<pt<=100)
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.1 (p.36): '>85% for ESC_T > 10 GeV'; Fig.23a (|eta|<0.8): reco eff rises from ~0.85-0.90 at 10 GeV plateauing near ~0.95-0.99 for ESC_T > 20-30 GeV
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read ~0.95 plateau (barrel, ESC_T >~20 GeV); ~0.85-0.90 in the 10-20 GeV ramp
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.95 +/- ~0.03)
coefficients.rationale: Plateau barrel reconstruction efficiency read from Fig.23a is ~0.95, consistent with the card's 0.95. The single flat 0.95 over 1-100 GeV is optimistic at the low end (10-20 GeV ramp is ~0.85-0.90) but matches the dominant high-pT plateau. Add ~3% total uncertainty.

coefficients.name: eff_barrel_highpt (|eta|<=1.5, pt>100)
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.1 (p.36) + Fig.23a: barrel reco efficiency plateaus near unity at high ESC_T; uncertainty '<1% as ESC_T increases'
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read ~0.97-0.99 (barrel, high ESC_T plateau)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.99 +/- ~0.01)
coefficients.rationale: High-pT barrel reconstruction efficiency plateaus near unity in Fig.23a; card 0.99 is consistent. Attach <1% uncertainty per Sec 6.1.

coefficients.name: eff_endcap_lowpt (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, 0.1<pt<=1.0)
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.1 / Fig.23b only down to ESC_T ~5-10 GeV; this sub-GeV bin is outside measured range
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (no measurement below ~5 GeV)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.50), flag as unsourced low-pT assumption
coefficients.rationale: Card's 0.1-1.0 GeV endcap bin is below the CMS measured range; 1502.02701 provides no value here. 0.50 is an unmeasured assumption (plausible given harder endcap tracking, but unconfirmed).

coefficients.name: eff_endcap_midpt (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, 1.0<pt<=100)
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.1 (p.36): '>85% for ESC_T > 10 GeV, for all eta'; Fig.23b (1.57<|eta|<2): endcap reco eff ~0.85 at 10 GeV rising toward ~0.90-0.95 at higher ESC_T
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read ~0.85-0.90 (endcap plateau, 1.57<|eta|<2); >0.85 for ESC_T>10 GeV
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: ~few % (ESC_T<20 GeV), decreasing at high ESC_T; larger fluctuations in endcap
coefficients.proposed_revision: Revise to ~0.87 +/- 0.04 to match the measured >0.85 plateau (or retain 0.83 as a conservative eta-averaged value to 2.5)
coefficients.rationale: The paper states efficiency is >85% for ESC_T>10 GeV for ALL eta; card endcap 0.83 sits just below this floor, making it mildly pessimistic. However Fig.23b only reaches |eta|<2 (efficiency higher there) while the card bin extends to 2.5 where it likely degrades, so 0.83 is a defensible eta-averaged compromise. Propose ~0.87 +/- 0.04 if matching the measured plateau.

coefficients.name: eff_endcap_highpt (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>100)
coefficients.locator: Sec 6.1 (p.36) + Fig.23b: endcap reco efficiency approaches high values at high ESC_T; uncertainty <1% at high ESC_T
coefficients.extracted_value: plot-read ~0.90-0.97 (endcap high-ESC_T plateau, 1.57<|eta|<2)
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: <1% to few % at high ESC_T; endcap fluctuations larger
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.90 +/- ~0.03)
coefficients.rationale: High-pT endcap reconstruction efficiency from Fig.23b is in the ~0.90-0.97 range; card's 0.90 is consistent at the conservative end, reasonable given the card endcap extends to 2.5 (edge degradation). Attach ~3% uncertainty.

extractions.source_summary: Two authoritative CMS sources cover the HCal resolution formula. (1) Central/barrel-endcap (|eta|<=3.0): the combined ECAL+HCAL pion test-beam resolution sigma/E = 110%/sqrt(E) (+) 9%, stated in the CMS particle-flow paper "Particle-flow reconstruction and global event description with the CMS detector", JINST 12 (2017) P10003, arXiv:1706.04965, Sec. 3 Eq. (2), which cites the underlying test-beam measurement CMS HCAL/ECAL Collaboration, "The CMS barrel calorimeter response to particle beams from 2 to 350 GeV/c", Eur. Phys. J. C 60 (2009) 359 (arXiv:0901.4118). The CMS HCAL prototype/design target (hep-ex/0007045) quotes 120-122%/sqrt(E) (+) 5%. (2) Forward HF (3.0<|eta|<=5.0): CMS Collaboration, "Design, performance, and calibration of CMS forward calorimeter wedges", Eur. Phys. J. C 53 (2008) 139 (arXiv:0706.3727) / CMS HCAL TDR (CERN/LHCC 97-31), giving the HF HADRONIC resolution a=280%/sqrt(E) (+) 11% (and EM 198%/sqrt(E) (+) 9%). These are peer-reviewed / collaboration-endorsed. Note: the Delphes card stores resolution in absolute-energy form sigma_E = sqrt(C^2*E^2 + S^2*E + N^2), so C is the constant (fractional) term and S is the stochastic coefficient (relative term S/sqrt(E)); N (noise) is set to 0 in both HCal regions.

coefficients.name: C_central (constant term, |eta|<=3.0)
coefficients.applicability: HCal central region, |eta| <= 3.0; multiplies energy^2 inside sqrt, i.e. constant (fractional) term C = 5%
coefficients.locator: arXiv:1706.04965 (JINST 12 (2017) P10003), Sec. 3, Eq. (2): combined ECAL+HCAL sigma/E = 110%/sqrt(E) (+) 9%; underlying measurement Eur. Phys. J. C 60 (2009) 359 (arXiv:0901.4118). Design value hep-ex/0007045: 122%/sqrt(E) (+) 5%.
coefficients.extracted_value: constant term = 9% (0.09) measured combined ECAL+HCAL; 5% (0.05) design/prototype target
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: PF paper quotes no explicit error on Eq.(2); test-beam fits give constant term ~4.0-6.5% +/- 0.1% depending on config (hep-ex/0007045)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (0.050); optionally cite design value 5% (hep-ex/0007045 / HCAL design) as source. If matching the PF combined measurement instead, 0.09 would be the value.
coefficients.rationale: Card uses 5% constant term, which matches the CMS HCAL design target (120-122%/sqrt(E) (+) 5%) but is below the measured combined ECAL+HCAL constant term of 9% in the PF paper. Consistent with design spec; optimistic vs measured combined resolution.

coefficients.name: S_central (stochastic term, |eta|<=3.0)
coefficients.applicability: HCal central region, |eta| <= 3.0; multiplies energy inside sqrt, i.e. stochastic coefficient S = 150%/sqrt(E)
coefficients.locator: arXiv:1706.04965, Sec. 3, Eq. (2): sigma/E = 110%/sqrt(E) (+) 9%. Design: hep-ex/0007045 abstract/Sec. (CMS barrel design) sigma_E/E = 122%/sqrt(E) (+) 5% and '120%/sqrt(E) (+) 5% for single incident hadrons'.
coefficients.extracted_value: 110% (1.10) measured combined ECAL+HCAL; 120-122% (1.20-1.22) HCAL design target
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: no explicit error on PF Eq.(2); individual test-beam fits 82-127% +/- ~1% across configs (hep-ex/0007045)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Revise to ~1.10 (with constant 0.09) to match the CMS-measured combined ECAL+HCAL resolution sigma/E=110%/sqrt(E)(+)9% [arXiv:1706.04965 Eq.2]; or 1.20-1.22 if using the HCAL design target. Card's 1.50 is not directly supported by any quoted CMS fit.
coefficients.rationale: Card uses 150%/sqrt(E), ~36% larger than the measured 110% (PF paper) and ~23% larger than the 120-122% design value. No public CMS source gives 150% for the central combined calorimeter; the card single-particle value is more pessimistic than the published combined resolution.

coefficients.name: C_HF (constant term, 3.0<|eta|<=5.0)
coefficients.applicability: HCal forward HF region, 3.0 < |eta| <= 5.0; constant (fractional) term C = 13%
coefficients.locator: CMS Collaboration, 'Design, performance, and calibration of CMS forward calorimeter wedges', Eur. Phys. J. C 53 (2008) 139 (arXiv:0706.3727); CMS HCAL TDR (CERN/LHCC 97-31): HF HADRONIC resolution a=280%/sqrt(E) (+) b=11%; HF EM 198%/sqrt(E) (+) 9%.
coefficients.extracted_value: 11% (0.11) hadronic constant term (HF); 9% (0.09) electromagnetic constant term
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: TDR/design parametrization; quoted without explicit per-term error in the summary (order ~1%)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Revise toward 0.11 to match the measured HF hadronic constant term (11%) [arXiv:0706.3727 / HCAL TDR]; current 0.13 is slightly pessimistic.
coefficients.rationale: Card uses 13% constant term for HF; the published HF hadronic resolution has 11%. Close but ~2 percentage points higher (slightly pessimistic); recommend 0.11 to match source.

coefficients.name: S_HF (stochastic term, 3.0<|eta|<=5.0)
coefficients.applicability: HCal forward HF region, 3.0 < |eta| <= 5.0; stochastic coefficient S = 270%/sqrt(E)
coefficients.locator: CMS Collaboration, 'Design, performance, and calibration of CMS forward calorimeter wedges', Eur. Phys. J. C 53 (2008) 139 (arXiv:0706.3727); CMS HCAL TDR: HF HADRONIC a=280%/sqrt(E) (+) 11%.
coefficients.extracted_value: 280% (2.80) HF hadronic stochastic term
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: design/TDR parametrization, no explicit error in summary (~few %)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Optionally revise to 2.80 to exactly match the measured HF hadronic stochastic term [arXiv:0706.3727 / HCAL TDR]; current 2.70 is within ~4% and effectively consistent.
coefficients.rationale: Card uses 270%/sqrt(E); the published HF hadronic value is 280%/sqrt(E). Within ~4%, clearly tracing to the HF hadronic resolution; consistent, with a minor optional tweak to 2.80 for exactness.

extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card uses two HCal regions: |eta|<=3.0 (central, single combined ECAL+HCAL parametrization) and 3.0<|eta|<=5.0 (HF). The authoritative central source (PF paper Eq.2 / test beam) is a single barrel/endcap combined number with NO eta dependence quoted, so it covers |eta|<3 only approximately and does not separately validate the endcap. The HF source (forward wedges paper / HCAL TDR) nominally covers 3<|eta|<5, matching the card's HF region. No finer eta binning is available in the sources to match the card's two-bin split; the central 5%/150% values are not reproduced by any single published CMS fit (measured 9%/110%, design 5%/120-122%).

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Jet energy scale and resolution in the CMS experiment in pp collisions at 8 TeV", JINST 12 (2017) P02014, arXiv:1607.03663 (DOI 10.1088/1748-0221/12/02/P02014). This is the collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed reference for CMS jet energy scale (JES) corrections and uncertainties at 8 TeV (19.7 fb^-1). Key results extracted directly from the full text (pypdf extraction of arXiv:1607.03663v2): abstract / Sec. 1 (txt lines 22-28, 290-293) state final JES uncertainties are below 3% across pT>30 GeV, |eta|<5.0; below 1% in the barrel (|eta|<1.3) for pT>30 GeV when excluding flavor uncertainties; minimum 0.32% for pT~165-330 GeV, |eta|<0.8. Resolution NSC parametrization sigma_pT/pT = sqrt(sgn(N)N^2/pT^2 + S^2/pT + C^2) is Eq. (38), Sec. 8 (txt lines 3737-3748), with reference resolutions in Fig. 36 and eta-binned data/MC scale factors (Sec. 8). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the Delphes EnergyScale ScaleFormula is a multiplicative jet-momentum *scale-correction* factor, whereas this paper's headline numbers are JES *uncertainties* and the JER (resolution) is a separate quantity; the paper does not publish the specific closed-form sqrt((a-b|eta|)^2/pT+1) used in the card.

coefficients.name: ScaleFormula_jet
coefficients.current_value: sqrt( (2.5 - 0.15*(abs(eta)))^2 / pt + 1.0 )  (full closed-form multiplicative jet energy-scale correction; coefficients a=2.5, b=0.15, offset=1.0)
coefficients.applicability: All jets from FastJetFinder/jets; pt in GeV; eta dependence linear in |eta|. Card applies it over the full jet acceptance (no explicit eta/pt bounds in this module).
coefficients.locator: Abstract / Sec. 1 (arXiv:1607.03663v2, extracted-text lines 22-28 and 290-293): total JES uncertainty <3% for pT>30 GeV, |eta|<5.0; <1% in barrel |eta|<1.3 for pT>30 GeV (excl. flavor); 0.32% at pT~165-330 GeV. Resolution form Eq. (38), Sec. 8 (lines 3737-3748). No table gives the card's a=2.5/b=0.15/offset=1.0 closed form.
coefficients.extracted_value: not-tabulated (no closed-form sqrt((a-b|eta|)^2/pT+1) scale formula appears in the paper). Closest published magnitudes: residual JES correction/uncertainty is a few % at pT~30-100 GeV and sub-% at high pT. Numerical evaluation of the card formula at eta=0: pT=30 GeV -> factor 1.099 (+9.9%); pT=100 GeV -> 1.031 (+3.1%); pT=1000 GeV -> 1.003 (+0.3%).
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: JES uncertainty (not the correction itself): <3% for pT>30 GeV |eta|<5.0; <1% in barrel for pT>30 GeV (excl. flavor); min 0.32% at pT~165-330 GeV |eta|<0.8 (abstract, lines 22-28).
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (as a generic order-of-magnitude Delphes default), BUT flag as no-source for the exact coefficients. The functional form sqrt((2.5-0.15|eta|)^2/pT+1) and the constants 2.5, 0.15, 1.0 are the long-standing Delphes generic default and are NOT derived from arXiv:1607.03663 or any published CMS measurement. Recommended for the JINST provenance paper: either (a) document it explicitly as a Delphes-default placeholder with no measured provenance, or (b) replace with a parametrization tied to the published CMS JES residual-correction/uncertainty (<3% pT>30 GeV; <1% barrel pT>30 GeV; ~0.3% at high pT, |eta|<0.8) plus an explicit uncertainty band. No public source supplies the specific a=2.5, b=0.15 coefficients.
coefficients.rationale: The single hard-coded ScaleFormula is the Delphes generic-default energy-scale correction; its closed form and constants (2.5, 0.15, 1.0) are not published in arXiv:1607.03663 nor any CMS JES paper, so the exact coefficients have no traceable source (arxiv=none-found for the coefficients themselves). Its numerical magnitude (~+10% at pT=30, ~+3% at pT=100, ~+0.3% at pT=1000, eta=0) is broadly the right order vs the measured CMS residual-correction/uncertainty scale (<3% for pT>30 GeV, sub-% at high pT), so it is not grossly wrong, but it cannot be claimed as sourced and should be documented as a placeholder or re-derived from the cited paper with an uncertainty band.

extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: The card uses a single continuous linear-in-|eta| dependence (coefficient 0.15 per unit |eta|) with no binning and no pt boundaries. The CMS source provides JES uncertainties and JER in discrete eta bins (notably barrel |eta|<1.3, and finer bins out to |eta|<5.2) and as functions of pT, not as a single sqrt((a-b|eta|)^2/pT+1) form. There is therefore a structural form/binning mismatch: the card's continuous closed form cannot be matched bin-by-bin to any single table/figure in arXiv:1607.03663.

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Performance of the CMS muon detector and muon reconstruction with proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV" (analysis code MUO-16-001), JINST 13 (2018) P06015, arXiv:1804.04528, 2018. Authoritative because it is the CMS-endorsed, peer-reviewed (JINST) muon-performance paper measuring the reco+ID efficiency of the standard cut-based Loose/Medium/Tight muon selections via tag-and-probe on Z->mumu data and simulation at 13 TeV. Key results: Table 3 (eff. for pT>20 GeV, two |eta| regions 0.0-0.9 and 0.9-2.4) and Figure 7 (eps_reco+ID vs eta for Loose and Tight muons, pT>=20 GeV). Loose ID >99% over the full eta range (Sec. 6, line 887). Tight ID varies 95-99% depending on eta (line 890).
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Binning mismatch on BOTH axes. (1) Eta: card splits acceptance at |eta|=1.5 (two bins: <=1.5 and 1.5-2.4), but the source (Table 3 / Fig. 7) bins at |eta|=0.9 (regions 0.0-0.9 and 0.9-2.4). The card's barrel/endcap boundary does not correspond to any source boundary. (2) pT: card turn-on threshold is pt>10 GeV, but the source efficiencies in Table 3 are all quoted for pT>20 GeV; the paper explicitly measures vs pT only over 20-200 GeV (line 888-889) where Loose is flat within 1%, so the card's 10-20 GeV plateau is an extrapolation not directly supported by tabulated numbers (efficiency falls below the plateau near the 10 GeV turn-on). The card's outer edge |eta|=2.4 matches the source acceptance (|eta|<2.4) correctly.

coefficients.name: eff_lowpt_turnon
coefficients.locator: Sec. 6 'Muon reconstruction and identification efficiency', text lines ~888-889 (efficiency measured/flat over pT 20-200 GeV); Fig. 7 caption (pT>=20 GeV). No tabulated value below 20 GeV.

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Performance of the CMS muon detector and muon reconstruction with proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV," JINST 13 (2018) P06015, arXiv:1804.04528 (2018). Authoritative collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed measurement of muon reconstruction/identification efficiency vs eta and pT using the tag-and-probe method on 2015/2016 13 TeV pp data. Relevant content: Sec. 5 (line ~317: "about 99% of the muons produced within the geometrical acceptance of the muon system [|eta|<2.4] are reconstructed either as a global muon track or as a tracker muon track"); Sec. 6.2 reco+ID efficiency, Fig. 7 (Loose/Tight ID efficiency vs eta, pT>20 GeV) with text "loose ID efficiency exceeds 99% over the entire eta range" and "constant with fluctuations well within 1%" in 20-200 GeV; Table 3 (Loose ID data eff. 99.75+/-0.02% for 0<|eta|<0.9 and 99.77+/-0.02% for 0.9<|eta|<2.4). This paper measures efficiency only down to pT~20 GeV (low-pT bins suffer large combinatorial background) and reports NO reconstruction-efficiency roll-off at high pT; for pT>200 GeV it improves momentum resolution (Sec. 7), not reco efficiency.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card eta binning is |eta|<=1.5, 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, |eta|>2.5. Source uses muon-system acceptance |eta|<2.4 and bins efficiency as 0<|eta|<0.9 / 0.9<|eta|<2.4 (Table 3), with Fig. 7 showing full eta-dependent shape. Two mismatches: (1) card boundary at 1.5 has no counterpart in the source (which splits at 0.9); (2) card extends acceptance to |eta|=2.5 whereas CMS muon-system acceptance is |eta|<2.4, so the card's 0.98 plateau region slightly overshoots the measured acceptance edge.

coefficients.locator: arXiv:1804.04528 (JINST 13 (2018) P06015): efficiency vs pT shown only for pT>=20 GeV (Fig. 7/Fig. 8, Table 3); Sec. 6.2 notes large combinatorial background and large uncertainties in low-pT bins. No measured value at 0.1-1 GeV.

coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current (provisionally); no public CMS source measures muon tracking efficiency in the 0.1-1 GeV bin, so this value cannot be confirmed or revised from the literature.
coefficients.rationale: The cited CMS paper measures muon reco+ID efficiency only for pT>=20 GeV; the 0.1-1 GeV turn-on value 0.75 is not measured there nor in any located public CMS source, so it cannot be reconciled.

extractions.source_summary: Primary authoritative source: CMS Collaboration, "Electron and photon reconstruction and identification with the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC," JINST 16 (2021) P05014, arXiv:2012.06888 (Run 2, 13 TeV, 136 fb-1). Section 7.2.1 states the cut-based photon identification working points have average signal efficiencies of about 90% (loose), 80% (medium), 70% (tight); Fig. 27 shows the loose cut-based and loosest BDT-based photon ID efficiency vs photon ET in four eta ranges, with data/MC ratios within 5% of unity (endcap, low/medium-ET region most affected by ECAL-noise sigma_ieta_ieta effects). Supporting/earlier source: CMS Collaboration, "Performance of photon reconstruction and identification with the CMS detector in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=8 TeV," JINST 10 (2015) P08010, arXiv:1502.02702; Table 3 (loose/medium/tight cut-based requirements) and Fig. 18 (sequential-cut photon ID efficiency vs eta, n_PU, and pT for the three working points, including electron veto). Both are CMS collaboration-endorsed, peer-reviewed (JINST). Neither paper tabulates a single per-(eta,pt) reco-efficiency number matching the Delphes step form; the card values are effective/idealized reco+ID efficiencies that must be benchmarked against the loose-WP average (~90%) and the qualitative barrel>endcap pattern in Figs. 18/27.
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Significant binning mismatch. Card uses two eta bins (|eta|<=1.5; 1.5<|eta|<=2.5) with a single pt threshold (pt>10 GeV) and flat efficiencies. Sources do NOT use these bins: arXiv:2012.06888 Fig. 27 uses four eta ranges (typically EB low-eta, EB high-eta, EE low-eta, EE high-eta with the EB/EE boundary at the ECAL crack |eta|~1.479-1.566) and reports efficiency as a continuous function of ET (no flat pt>10 plateau is tabulated); arXiv:1502.02702 Fig. 18 is continuous in eta and pT. The card's barrel/endcap split at 1.5 approximates the ECAL boundary (1.479) but ignores the 1.4442-1.566 transition gap (excluded crack) and the per-bin/per-WP and pT-dependent variation. No single number in either source is binned exactly as the card; values must be read as plateau approximations of the loose-WP curves.

coefficients.name: eff_endcap (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>10)
coefficients.locator: Sec. 7.2.1 (loose cut-based WP avg ~90%, with explicit note endcap low/medium-ET sigma_ieta_ieta affected by ECAL noise); Fig. 27 left (endcap eta ranges, lower efficiency than barrel)

coefficients.name: eff_forward (|eta|>2.5)

extractions.source_summary: CMS Collaboration, "Performance of reconstruction and identification of tau leptons decaying to hadrons and nu_tau in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV," JINST 13 (2018) P10005, arXiv:1809.02816 (2016 data, 35.9 fb^-1). This is the authoritative CMS HPS + MVA-isolation tau-ID performance paper. It defines the jet-rejection isolation working points and quantifies the genuine-tau identification efficiency vs the jet->tau_h misidentification probability (Sec. 5.2, Figs. 2-4) and the data-to-simulation scale factors (Table 3). It is the source that backs the Delphes flat tau eff=0.6 / jet mistag=0.01 numbers. The card itself currently cites no reference for these two numbers (audit_CMS.md line 78 marks them "Source needed (CMS tau ID WP)").
extractions.eta_binning_mismatch: Card uses a single flat efficiency over the full acceptance (TauEtaMax=2.5, TauPTMin=1 GeV); the source measures efficiency and mistag for tau_h/jets with pT>20 GeV and |eta|<2.3 (Sec.5.2, Fig.2/3 captions). Mismatches: (i) card eta reach 2.5 vs source 2.3; (ii) card pT floor 1 GeV vs source pT>20 GeV (no measurement below ~20 GeV, where efficiency turns on, Fig.4 left); (iii) card is flat in pT/eta whereas both eff and mistag have strong pT dependence (mistag falls from ~0.2% at low pT to ~0.07% at high pT for the tight WP, line 948; eff turns on below ~30 GeV, Fig.4).

coefficients.name: tau_eff_hadronic
coefficients.applicability: genuine hadronic tau (PDG 15), all pT>1 GeV, |eta|<2.5 (flat)
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5.2, lines describing MVA-isolation WPs ('isolation efficiencies between 40 and 90%, in steps of 10%'); Fig. 3 (eff vs mistag curve); Fig. 4 left (eff vs pT for VLoose..VVTight); Table 3 (data/MC scale factors); efficiency defined for tau_h with pT>20 GeV, |eta|<2.3
coefficients.extracted_value: 0.6 is a valid operating point: MVA-isolation WPs are defined across 40-90% efficiency; ~60% corresponds to the Loose/Medium WP region. The most-used Tight WP is 49%. Data/MC scale factors for WPs near 60% eff: Loose 0.98, Medium 0.97 (Table 3).
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: +/-5% (Table 3 scale-factor uncertainty, incl. 3.9% tracking term added in quadrature); efficiency itself uniform in pT by construction above ~30 GeV but turns on below (Fig.4 left)
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current value 0.6, but assign uncertainty +/-0.05 (5%, from Table 3 scale factors) and document that it represents a Loose/Medium MVA WP for pT>~20 GeV, |eta|<2.3; ideally add a low-pT turn-on (eff->0 below ~20 GeV) rather than a flat 0.6 down to 1 GeV.
coefficients.rationale: 0.6 sits squarely inside the measured 40-90% WP range (Loose/Medium); data/MC scale factors of 0.97-0.98+/-0.05 confirm the chosen-efficiency WPs are reproduced in data, so flat 0.6 is a defensible central value with +/-5% uncertainty, though the card omits the documented sub-20-GeV turn-on and uses |eta|<2.5 vs source 2.3.

coefficients.name: jet_to_tau_mistag
coefficients.applicability: jets / all non-tau partons (default PDG 0), all pT>1 GeV, |eta|<2.5 (flat)
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5.2: 'tau_h selection efficiencies and jet->tau_h misidentification probabilities ... for the most commonly used working point (tight) ... are 49% and 0.21% ... For high pT, the expected misidentification probability drops to 0.07%'; Fig. 3 (mistag vs eff, QCD multijet, pT 20-100/1000 GeV); Fig. 4 right (mistag vs jet pT)
coefficients.extracted_value: At ~60% tau eff (the card's operating point), the MVA-based jet->tau_h mistag from Fig.3 is ~1e-3 (0.1-0.3%); the older cut-based isolation-sum reaches ~0.5-1% only at lower efficiency. Tight WP (49% eff): 0.21% low/med pT, 0.07% high pT.
coefficients.extracted_uncertainty: strong pT dependence (factor ~3 from low to high pT); no single quoted symmetric uncertainty - read from Fig.3/Fig.4 plot (~plot-read)
coefficients.proposed_revision: Revise downward to ~0.003 (0.3%) for a 60%-efficiency modern MVA/DeepTau-style WP, with a pT-decreasing trend (~0.2% low pT -> ~0.07% high pT). Card's 0.01 is ~3-10x too high for the matched 60% eff point.
coefficients.rationale: Reading Fig.3 at the card's 0.6 tau efficiency gives jet mistag ~1e-3, and the explicit numbers (0.21%/0.07% at the 49% tight WP) bracket the 0.6 WP near a few x1e-3; the card's flat 0.01 overstates the fake rate by roughly a factor 3-10 and ignores the documented fall-off with pT.

coefficients.name: TauTagging_DeltaR
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5.2 / Eq.(6)-(7) and Table 3 caption: HPS isolation/signal cone and tau reconstruction use DeltaR=0.5 (isolation cone), e.g. 'MVA-based discriminant with DeltaR = 0.5' (Table 3 caption)
coefficients.extracted_value: DeltaR=0.5 is the CMS HPS isolation cone size used in the reference (Table 3 caption explicitly states DeltaR=0.5).
coefficients.proposed_revision: keep current
coefficients.rationale: The matching/cone DeltaR=0.5 in the card matches the CMS HPS isolation cone DeltaR=0.5 used in 1809.02816 (Table 3 caption); this is an algorithmic configuration choice with no associated measured uncertainty.

coefficients.name: TauTagging_TauEtaMax
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5.2 / Fig.2-3 captions: efficiency and mistag evaluated for |eta|<2.3 (tracker+HPS acceptance)
coefficients.extracted_value: Source restricts tau_h measurements to |eta|<2.3; card uses 2.5.
coefficients.proposed_revision: Consider tightening to |eta|<2.3 to match the CMS measured tau_h acceptance in 1809.02816 (Sec.5.2); else document that 2.4-2.5 is an extrapolation beyond the measured region.
coefficients.rationale: The card applies the flat efficiency out to |eta|<2.5, but the source only measures tau_h performance to |eta|<2.3; the 2.3-2.5 region is unmeasured, so the card slightly over-extends the acceptance.

coefficients.name: TauTagging_TauPTMin
coefficients.locator: Sec. 5.2 / Fig.2-4 captions: tau_h efficiency and jet mistag evaluated for pT>20 GeV (generated tau matched to reco tau pT>18 GeV)
coefficients.extracted_value: Source measures performance only for tau_h pT>20 GeV; below ~20-30 GeV the efficiency turns on from 0 (Fig.4 left). Card applies flat 0.6 down to 1 GeV.
coefficients.proposed_revision: Keep the loose tagging threshold but do NOT apply the flat 0.6 efficiency below ~20 GeV; the source shows the efficiency turns on around 20-30 GeV (Fig.4 left), so a flat 0.6 from 1 GeV overestimates low-pT tau efficiency.
coefficients.rationale: The reference does not validate tau-ID below pT=20 GeV and shows a turn-on (Fig.4 left); the card's flat 0.6 efficiency down to TauPTMin=1 GeV overstates efficiency in the unmeasured low-pT region.

per_coefficient.name: light_mistag_PDG0_const
per_coefficient.note: Source/locator verified COLD. arXiv:1907.05120 Table 4 (p.11-12 of PDF), MV2 row eps_b=70%: 'Selection >0.83 ... Light-flavour jet [rejection] 300' (c-jet 8.9). So source light-rejection 300 -> mistag 1/300=0.0033 is correct. Table 4/Fig.2 caption confirms inclusive selection '|eta|<=2.5, Jet pT >= 20 GeV'. Independently recomputed the card formula 0.002+7.3e-06*pt: gives mistag 0.0021 (pt20), 0.0024 (pt50), 0.0035 (pt200) -> rejection 466/423/289, bracketing 300. Low-pT asymptote 0.002 as claimed. Extracted value and 'consistent / keep current' verdict are supported.

per_coefficient.name: light_mistag_PDG0_slope

Verified card numerics: at pt=1000 GeV light mistag = 0.0093, rejection = 107.5 -- matches the extraction's '~0.0093 at 1 TeV (rejection ~107)' exactly. Rising mistag / falling light-rejection vs pT is qualitatively consistent with Fig.2(a) trend in 1907.05120. No public tabulated slope exists; 'keep current' justified. (Minor: Fig.2 in the source is rejection-vs-eps_b at fixed inclusive pt>=20 GeV, not a pT-dependence plot; the pT shape is asserted by the card fit, not directly liftable from Fig.2.)

per_coefficient.name: c_mistag_PDG4_amplitude
per_coefficient.note: arXiv:1907.05120 Table 4, MV2 eps_b=70%: c-jet rejection = 8.9 -> c-mistag 1/8.9 = 0.112, exactly as extracted. Independently recomputed card 0.20*tanh(0.02*pt)*(1/(1+0.0034*pt)): peak c-mistag = 0.144 near pt~85-100 GeV -> rejection ~6.9 (extraction said ~7), falls to ~0.074 (rej ~13.5) at 500 GeV. Card is mildly pessimistic on c-rejection at the peak (6.9 vs measured inclusive 8.9) but same order. 'consistent / keep current' supported; the optional suggestion to lower amplitude to ~0.16 for exact-WP match is arithmetically reasonable.

per_coefficient.name: c_mistag_PDG4_turnon

Verified resulting profile: c-mistag rises through 0.097 (pt30) to plateau 0.13-0.144 over pt~50-150 GeV, i.e. rejection ~7-10, consistent with Table 4 inclusive c-rejection 8.9. Source Fig.8 is b-jet efficiency vs pT for the 70% MV2 OP (confirmed p.22-23 caption); it is a b-eff plot, not a c-efficiency-vs-pT plot, so the locator 'Fig.8 (b/c efficiency vs pT)' slightly overstates what Fig.8 shows (b-eff only), but the Table 4 anchor is correct and the verdict holds.

per_coefficient.name: b_eff_PDG5_amplitude

The source (1907.05120, p.23, summarizing Table 5) actually states: 'The total uncertainty reaches about 1% for 40 GeV <= pT < 250 GeV ... verifications.corrections:
Two descriptive (non-coefficient) errors in source_summary; no coefficient value, locator, or verdict needs to change.

1) TITLE MISLABEL: source_summary titles arXiv:1404.4562 as 'Measurement of the muon reconstruction performance of the ATLAS detector using 2010 LHC pp collision data...'. That is wrong. arXiv:1404.4562's actual title is 'Muon reconstruction efficiency and momentum resolution of the ATLAS experiment in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV in 2010'. The 'Measurement of the muon reconstruction performance...' title actually belongs to the SEPARATE 2011/2012 paper arXiv:1407.3935 (EPJC 74:3130). The extraction conflated the two papers' titles. (Verified via arxiv.org/abs/1404.4562 and the rendered PDF.)

2) JOURNAL-REF FORENSICS DIRECTION CONFIRMED, with the correct ref now pinned: arXiv:1404.4562 = EPJC 74 (2014) 3034 (DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-014-3034-9). arXiv:1407.3935 = EPJC 74 (2014) 3130 (DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-014-3130-x). The extraction's core claim is therefore CORRECT: the card muon-block comment (line 184) that writes 'arXiv:1404.4562 (EPJC 74 (2014) 3130)' pairs the 2010 paper's arXiv ID with the WRONG journal ref (3130 belongs to the 2011/2012 paper); the right journal ref for 1404.4562 is EPJC 74:3034. This card-comment defect propagates from the adjacent MuonMomentumSmearing provenance and is a real provenance bug worth fixing in the card.

3) Minor locator note: Eq.(2) is on printed page 18 (PDF page 19), and Figs.17/18 on printed pages 20/21 (PDF pages 21/22); the extraction's '(p.18-19)' for Eq.(2) is close enough (the equation sits at the top of printed p.18). Not a substantive error.

All six (a,b) plot-read values, the 5%/10% material statement, the 'a_ID set to MC' and 'b_ID from Z->mumu' attributions, the pT/tan^2(theta) form for |eta|>2.0, the eta-region labels (|eta|<1.05, 1.05-1.7, 1.7-2.0, 2.0-2.5), the not-tabulated caveat, and the 'card numbers are generic Delphes defaults, not lifted, card-pessimistic vs muon-ID' conclusions are all CONFIRMED against the primary source. No better public source with a liftable charged-hadron (a,b) table exists; these are the standard Delphes ATLAS-card defaults.

per_coefficient.name: eff_pt_below_0p1_threshold
per_coefficient.note: Source cited correctly and locator is real. The paper's selection is 'particles with transverse momentum greater than 500 MeV and absolute pseudorapidity less than 2.5' (p.2 abstract; Sec 3: 'pT, of at least 500 MeV'; Sec 4 track selection: 'pT > 500 MeV and |η| < 2.5'). Fig 2(d) (confirmed by caption: 'the eﬃciency as a function of (d) transverse momentum, pT') has a pT axis starting near 0.5 GeV; the pT<0.1 GeV region is genuinely below the measured range. The extraction correctly reports this is not tabulated and that the 0.00 acceptance floor below 0.1 GeV is a non-cited convention. Verdict CANNOT-DETERMINE / 'keep current' is appropriate and honestly stated. I confirm no better public number for pT<0.1 GeV exists in this paper.

per_coefficient.name: eff_central_lowpt
per_coefficient.note: Locator correct: Fig 2(d) is eff vs pT (caption line: 'after this correction as a function of (c) η and (d) transverse momentum, pT'). Fig 2(d) y-axis is 0.76-0.94; the curve rises from low values near pT=0.5 GeV. The extraction's plot-read ~0.78 at 0.5-1 GeV is consistent with the axis range (lowest tick 0.76). The card bin 0.1-1.0 GeV extends below the measured 0.5 GeV floor, so it is genuinely partly unmeasured. CANNOT-DETERMINE is the right verdict. NOTE on uncertainty wording: the cited '3.5% at pT=500 MeV' is f_okr (the fraction of selected tracks whose primary is OUT of the kinematic range, relevant only for 2.4<|η|<2.5; p.10 'estimated... to be 3.5% at pT = 500 MeV, decreasing to 1% for pT = 1 GeV'), NOT a tracking efficiency systematic. The '~0.7%' central systematic is real (Sec 6.3: 'total uncertainty due to the imperfect knowledge of the detector material is ±0.7% in the most central region'). Mild mislabeling of the 3.5% term but the value and direction of the conclusion stand.

per_coefficient.name: eff_central_highpt
per_coefficient.note: Strongly confirmed. Fig 2(d) (eff vs pT) y-axis runs only 0.76 to 0.94 (tick labels: 0.76,0.78,0.80,0.82,0.84,0.86,0.88,0.90,0.92,0.94) — the measured efficiency CANNOT reach the card's 0.95 because 0.95 is literally off the top of the plotted axis. per_coefficient.name: eff_forward_lowpt
per_coefficient.note: Locator correct: Fig 2(c) is eff vs η (caption), forward region 1.5<|η|<2.5. per_coefficient.name: eff_forward_highpt
per_coefficient.note: Fig 2(c) (eff vs η, axis 0.6-1.0) plus Sec 6.3 text ('lower in the region |η| > 1 due to particles passing through more material'; local rise at |η|~2.2) support the extraction's forward band of roughly 0.65-0.80 (eta-average ~0.73). Card 0.101/0.0017 (EM) and 0.285/0.0350 (FCal) match physics/0608012 Eq.8+Fig.19 (10.1±0.1 %·√GeV, 0.17±0.04 %) and arXiv:2109.02551 Table 4 (EM 10.1%/0.2%, FCal 28.5%/3.5%) exactly. per_coefficient.name: eff_lowpt_pt_le_10
per_coefficient.note: Source (arXiv:1902.04655v2 = EPJC 79 (2019) 639, verified title 'Electron reconstruction and identification in the ATLAS experiment...') confirms finite ID efficiency below 10 GeV. Rationale and proposed revision are justified by the source.

per_coefficient.name: C_const_hec_endcap
per_coefficient.note: I read physics/0407026 full PDF (pdfminer). The standalone-HEC noise-subtracted pion resolution is stated as sigma(E)/E = (0.841 +- 0.003)/sqrt(E/GeV) (+) constant (Sec. 8/RESPONSE TO PIONS, near 'The noise subtracted energy resolution for pions'). The text fragments around the figure prevented cleanly isolating the standalone pion CONSTANT term; the paper mentions combined-system terms like '(72.3 +- 0.9)% sqrt(GeV)' and 'non-vanishing constant terms'. I could NOT locate a clean '(5.0 +- 0.3)%' standalone-HEC constant in this paper as the extraction's locator claims. The card C=5.0% may indeed be the canonical HEC design constant, but the cited paper's stochastic term is 84.1%, not the 78% the extraction attributes to it, casting doubt on the whole (78/5.0) attribution to physics/0407026. Verdict downgraded to CANNOT_CONFIRM pending a clean read of the standalone-HEC constant term.

per_coefficient.name: S_stochastic_hec_endcap
per_coefficient.note: REFUTES the extraction's locator value. physics/0407026 (read cold from PDF) states the standalone-HEC noise-subtracted PION resolution sampling term is sigma(E)/E = (0.841 +- 0.003)/sqrt(E/GeV), i.e. ~84.1%/sqrt(E) -- NOT the (78+-2)% the extraction attributes to this paper. The extraction's claim that physics/0407026 'reports pion sigma/E = (78+-2)%/sqrt(E) (+) (5.0+-0.3)%' is not supported by the paper's own text. Separately, the card value S=0.706 (70.6%) is below BOTH 84.1% (this paper) and the 78% the extraction quoted, so the extraction's broader conclusion (card is optimistic vs the canonical standalone HEC) still holds directionally; but the specific extracted_value 0.78 and its source attribution are wrong. verifications.corrections:
1) MAJOR (S_stochastic_hec_endcap): The extraction attributes 'pion sigma/E = (78+-2)%/sqrt(E) (+) (5.0+-0.3)%' to physics/0407026.
