per_coefficient.name: jes_stochastic_coeff_eta0 (the 3.0 in (3.0-0.2*abs(eta))^2)
per_coefficient.note: Card line 633 verified verbatim: 'set ScaleFormula { sqrt( (3.0 - 0.2*(abs(eta)))^2 / pt + 1.0 ) }'. All cited sources are real and locators accurate. arXiv:2007.02645 abstract (fetched) states verbatim '(24 +/- 1.5)% at 20 GeV to (6 +/- 0.5)% at 300 GeV'. Eq.(4) verified in PDF p.41: 'sigma(pT)/pT = N/pT (+) S/sqrt(pT) (+) C', with the constant term dominating above ~400 GeV. Fig.30(a) caption verified: 'relative jet energy resolution ... as a function of pT_jet', anti-kt R=0.4, '0.2 <= |eta| < 0.7' (central reference region, confirmed at line ~2523). arXiv:1210.6210 Eq.(7) verified verbatim ('N/pT (+) S/sqrt(pT) (+) C', noise/stochastic/constant) and Fig.8 ('Fractional jet pT resolution for the dijet balance and bisector methods') / Fig.13 ('Fractional jet pT resolutions ... anti-kt jets R=0.6 with |y|<0.8, 0.8<=|y|<1.2, 1.2<=|y|<2.1, 2.1<=|y|<2.8'). The 'card-wrong' verdict is justified: applied as an EnergyScale factor sqrt(9/pt+1), the formula yields +4.4% at 100 GeV and +20.4% at 20 GeV upward energy bias (I recomputed), versus ATLAS JES non-closure calibrated to <1% (100-500 GeV) and ~4.5% (20 GeV) per arXiv:1703.09665 abstract (fetched verbatim). No source supports 3.0 as a scale coefficient. CAVEAT: the implied S~0.7-0.9 sqrt(GeV) and the +/-0.05 uncertainty are figure-reads of Fig.30, not tabulated fitted values (the fitted N,S,C numbers do not appear in extractable text); and the rationale's '+15% at 20 GeV' is numerically off (actual +20.4%).

per_coefficient.name: jes_eta_slope (the 0.2 in 0.2*abs(eta))
per_coefficient.note: Card line 633 verified verbatim (0.2*abs(eta)). The rapidity bins cited for arXiv:1210.6210 Fig.13 are correct (|y|<0.8, 0.8<=|y|<1.2, 1.2<=|y|<2.1, 2.1<=|y|<2.8, verified in Fig.13 caption). arXiv:2007.02645 Fig.30(b) verified as 'relative jet energy resolution ... as a function of eta' at pT=30 GeV. The text of 2007.02645 confirms forward degradation ('for some pT ranges in more forward detector regions it can be significant', line ~3163; large non-closure at |eta|~3.2). The card formula has the coefficient inside (3.0-0.2|eta|)^2/pt, so it DECREASES with |eta|, implying improving resolution/bias forward -- which contradicts the measured worsening through the barrel-endcap transition. The 'card-wrong' verdict is justified. CAVEAT correctly flagged by the extraction: no source provides a single linear -0.2 sqrt(GeV)/|eta| slope; the eta dependence is figure-based and non-monotonic, so '0.2' is not a source-tabulated value -- it is an unsupported analytic parametrization, which is the basis for the verdict.

per_coefficient.name: jes_constant_asymptote (the +1.0 additive term inside sqrt)
per_coefficient.note: Card line 633 verified verbatim (+1.0 inside sqrt). For an EnergyScale module the +1.0 is the mandatory high-pT unity asymptote: sqrt(.../pt + 1.0) -> 1.0 as pt->infinity (I recomputed: factor=1.009 at 500 GeV, ->1.0). This matches ATLAS scale calibration to unity within <1% per arXiv:1703.09665 abstract ('less than 1% ... central calorimeter region |eta|<1.2 for jets with 100<pT<500 GeV', fetched verbatim). The distinction that this 1.0 is NOT the JER constant term C is correct: arXiv:2007.02645 Eq.(4) C term 'dominates the high-pT region, above approximately 400 GeV' (verified line ~2498). The 'consistent' verdict is justified. CAVEAT: the cross-check value C~0.04-0.05 is a figure-read of Fig.30(a)/inferred from the (6+/-0.5)% at 300 GeV abstract value; it is not stated as an inline fitted number in the source text. This does not affect the verdict since the proposed revision keeps 1.0 as required for the EnergyScale asymptote.

per_coefficient.name: pt_turnon_threshold
per_coefficient.note: Abstract confirms 'transverse momenta between 10 GeV and 1.5 TeV'. The measurement grid 'boundaries at 10, 15, 20, 25, ... 250 and 1500 GeV' confirms ET starts at 10 GeV. The card's instantaneous jump from 0 to the 0.95/0.85 plateau immediately above 10 GeV is indeed card-optimistic in the 10-40 GeV turn-on. Verdict and rationale supported.

Two of the six proposed revisions overstate the high-pT (slope) resolution by reading the 90% open-marker curve or the post-100 GeV tail instead of the 68% solid curve that the card's resolution definition should use:

Cold calibrated read of the SOLID 68% endcap marker at 100 GeV in Fig. 15 is ~7.0%, giving b~6.7e-4 GeV^-1. Recommended revision: a~0.019-0.023 (floor read ~1.9%), b~6.7e-4 (+/-1e-4) GeV^-1. (The ~10% figure is the 90% interval / tail.)

2) b_eta05_15_slope: extraction proposes b~4.2e-4 (from transition '~4-5% at 100 GeV'). The SOLID 68% transition marker at 100 GeV reads ~3.2% (b~2.8e-4); the ~4.5-5% is the 90% interval. If the card uses the 68% definition, b~2.8-3.0e-4 is more appropriate; if matching the abstract's 2.8% |eta|<1.4 average, ~4e-4 is acceptable. Flag as a 68%-vs-90% ambiguity, not a hard error.

Everything else verified correct: source paper (arXiv:1405.6569 on card line 154), Fig. 15 caption and eta-bin definitions (0-0.9 / 0.9-1.4 / 1.4-2.5), Fig. 14 reference, Sec. 5.2, the abstract '~2.8% in pT at pT=100 GeV, |eta|<1.4', the summary '~1.5% for 1<pT<10 GeV central', the module mechanics (MomentumSmearing.cc: res=formula output, pt=LogNormal(pt, res*pt), so a=0.06 means 6%), the eta-binning mismatch description, and all six 'card-pessimistic' verdicts. per_coefficient.note: Source has NO tabulated single number for the |eta|<=1.5, 0.1-1.0 GeV bin. Fig.8 (middle-right, barrel = eta 0-0.9) and Fig.10 (top-right) show a steep low-pT turn-on; text (Sec.5.1.2 lines): efficiency 'approximately constant for 1<pT<80 GeV, but, at small pT, the efficiency decreases quickly' and 'pion-nucleus cross section increases rapidly for pions of energies below 0.7 GeV.' The figure y-axis is unreadable from extracted text (no digitized values), so a 0.70 bin-average over 0.1-1.0 GeV cannot be exactly confirmed or refuted - it is a plausible but unverifiable plot-read. The extraction honestly marks matches_current='cannot-determine' and assigns ~10% plot-read spread; 'keep current' is defensible. Cannot independently confirm the exact 0.70 value from a tabulated source.

per_coefficient.name: eff_central_highpt
per_coefficient.note: Abstract: 'the average track-reconstruction efficiency ... pT > 0.9 GeV is 94% for ... |eta| < 0.9.' Text confirms 'approximately constant for 1<pT<80 GeV.' Source eta breakpoints (0-0.9 barrel, 0.9-1.4 transition; Fig.8 line) differ from card's 1.5 breakpoint, so the card's |eta|<=1.5 bin folds in the lower-efficiency 0.9-1.4 transition region; thus a bin-average is somewhat below the 94% barrel figure, making the card's 0.95 marginally optimistic (extraction verdict 'card-optimistic' is well-justified). The 0.94 anchor and ~2-3% uncertainty are supported by the quoted 94%. matches_current='yes' and the noted ~0.93 alternative are reasonable; net consistent within 1-2%.

per_coefficient.name: eff_forward_lowpt
per_coefficient.note: No tabulated number for the 1.5<|eta|<=2.5, 0.1-1.0 GeV bin. Fig.8 (middle-right, endcap = eta 1.4-2.5) and Fig.10 (top-right) show a steeper/lower low-pT turn-on in the forward region; supporting text: 'merging of separate trajectories ... more common in the region of the barrel to endcap transition and in the endcap regions ... large amounts of material' and 'up to 20% of the simulated pions are not reconstructed,' 'most significant for hadrons with pT <~ 700 MeV.' These qualitatively support a lower forward low-pT efficiency than barrel, but the exact 0.60 cannot be confirmed from any tabulated source (figure values not digitizable from text). Extraction marks 'cannot-determine' with ~10% spread; 'keep current' is defensible. Cannot independently confirm exact 0.60.

per_coefficient.name: eff_forward_highpt
per_coefficient.note: Abstract: 'the average track-reconstruction efficiency for promptly-produced charged particles with pT > 0.9 GeV is ... 85% for 0.9 < |eta| < 2.5.' The card forward bin 1.5<|eta|<=2.5 is a subset of the source's 0.9-2.5 average, and the card value 0.85 matches the quoted 85% directly. Locator (Abstract/Conclusions, Fig.8/Fig.10) and ~3% uncertainty are supported. Minor caveat: 1.5-2.5 excludes the higher-efficiency 0.9-1.5 part of the source average and keeps the lowest-efficiency highest-|eta| part, so 0.85 could even be slightly optimistic at the very forward edge - but it directly matches the quoted average and is well-supported. 'keep current' justified.

per_coefficient.name: eff_eta_outside_acceptance
per_coefficient.note: Conclusions: 'The tracking algorithms reconstruct tracks over the full pseudorapidity range of the tracker |eta| < 2.5.' Sec.5 methodology: 'simulated particles generated within |eta| < 2.5.' Fig.10 caption: 'The efficiency and fake rate plots are plotted for |eta| < 2.5.' Zero efficiency beyond |eta|=2.5 is exactly correct for this Run-1 tracker geometry. Locator and value accurate; 'keep current' justified.

verifications.corrections: No substantive corrections needed; all extracted claims are source-faithful. Minor locator notes (not errors): (1) The card breakpoint at |eta|=1.5 does NOT coincide with any source breakpoint - the source uses 0.9 (abstract average) and 0.9/1.4 (Fig.8 barrel/transition/endcap intervals 0-0.9, 0.9-1.4, 1.4-2.5). (4) eff_central_highpt: the 'card-optimistic' note (0.95 vs quoted 94% for |eta|<0.9, plus folding in the lower 0.9-1.4 transition) is correct and well-reasoned; the proposed ~0.93+/-0.02 alternative is a sound observation but 'keep current' is also acceptable given the coarse 2-region binning. No source/value/uncertainty error rises to the level of a required revision.

per_coefficient.name: barrel_prefactor_const

per_coefficient.name: barrel_prefactor_eta2_coeff

per_coefficient.name: endcap_prefactor_const

per_coefficient.name: endcap_prefactor_eta2_coeff
per_coefficient.note: Verified absence: '5.6' as a coefficient appears 0 times in 1306.2016 (searched '5.6%' and '5.6 '). No polynomial eta coefficient tabulated. Confirmed no-source; Delphes tuning constant.

per_coefficient.name: endcap_prefactor_eta_offset

per_coefficient.name: energy_shape_constant_C_barrel_endcap
per_coefficient.note: 1306.2016 Eq.(1) verified verbatim: 'sigma_E/E = 2.8%/sqrt(E(GeV)) (+) 12%/E(GeV) (+) 0.3%' with 'the three contributions correspond to the stochastic, noise, and constant terms.' per_coefficient.name: energy_shape_stochastic_S_barrel_endcap
per_coefficient.note: Eq.(1) stochastic term = 2.8%/sqrt(E), so S=0.028. Card hard-codes 0.11 (11%); '11%' appears 0 times in the paper. ~4x more pessimistic. per_coefficient.name: energy_shape_noise_N_barrel_endcap

per_coefficient.name: forward_HF_constant_C

per_coefficient.name: eff_pt_threshold_lowpt
per_coefficient.note: Paper quotes reco efficiency only 'in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV' (verbatim, Sec. 6 results text, PDF p.45: 'The reconstruction efficiency in the data ranges from 88% to 98% in the barrel and from 90% to 96% in the endcaps in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV.'). per_coefficient.name: eff_barrel_highpt
per_coefficient.note: Reco barrel value confirmed verbatim: 'ranges from 88% to 98% in the barrel ... in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV' (Sec. 6). Working points confirmed verbatim (Sec. 5.3): 'Three working points were originally designed to have average efficiencies of about 90, 80, and 70% for electrons from Z -> e+e- events, and were optimized separately for electrons in the ECAL barrel and endcaps.' per_coefficient.name: eff_endcap_highpt
per_coefficient.note: Reco endcap value confirmed verbatim: 'from 90% to 96% in the endcaps in the pT range from 10 to 100 GeV' (Sec. 6). Endcap ID efficiency ~84% confirmed: Fig. 17 text 'the sequential selection with respective efficiency for signal electrons of about 90% and 84%' (barrel/endcap). Combined reco(~0.95) x ID(~0.84-0.90) ~ 0.80-0.86 brackets the card's 0.85; 'consistent / matches-current yes' is correct.

per_coefficient.name: eff_acceptance_cutoff

Zero efficiency for |eta|>2.5 is correct; 'keep current' justified.

per_coefficient.name: eff_lowpt_floor (pt<=0.1 GeV)

per_coefficient.name: eff_barrel_lowpt (|eta|<=1.5, 0.1<pt<=1.0)

per_coefficient.name: eff_barrel_midpt (|eta|<=1.5, 1.0<pt<=100)
per_coefficient.note: TEXT FLOORS CONFIRMED but the specific plot-read plateau value is NOT verifiable cold. Verbatim text supports a lower bound only: Sec 6.1 'The efficiencies are found to be >85% for ESC_T > 10 GeV, for all eta' and 'SC reconstruction efficiency for ESC_T > 5 GeV is close to 100%.' Figure 23 is a vector plot; text extraction yields only axis labels (Efficiency 0.0-1.0; ESC_T 0-100 GeV), NOT the curve data points. per_coefficient.name: eff_barrel_highpt (|eta|<=1.5, pt>100)
per_coefficient.note: Uncertainty claim CONFIRMED: Sec 6.1 'decreasing to <1% as ESC_T increases.' The qualitative 'plateaus near unity' is consistent with 'SC reconstruction efficiency for ESC_T > 5 GeV is close to 100%.' However the precise plot-read '~0.97-0.99' cannot be confirmed from the extractable text (Fig.23 curve values not in text layer). Note: Fig.23 x-axis ends at 100 GeV, so pt>100 is at/just beyond the plotted range, making any precise read an extrapolation.

per_coefficient.name: eff_endcap_lowpt (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, 0.1<pt<=1.0)
per_coefficient.note: Extraction's 'no-source' verdict is correct. The 0.1-1.0 GeV endcap bin is below the measured range. Fig.23b covers 1.57<|eta|<2 only, and robust statements are for ESC_T>10 GeV. 0.50 is unmeasured by 1502.02701; correctly flagged as an unsourced low-pT assumption. No better public source found.

per_coefficient.name: eff_endcap_midpt (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, 1.0<pt<=100)
per_coefficient.note: The factual basis is verified verbatim: Sec 6.1 'The efficiencies are found to be >85% for ESC_T > 10 GeV, for all eta.' Card endcap 0.83 indeed sits just below this >85% floor, so the 'card-pessimistic' characterization is correct. CAVEAT confirmed: Fig.23b only reaches |eta|<2 ('1.57 < |eta| < 2', lines 3137/3242-3243), while the card bin extends to 2.5 (paper text line 230: tracks reconstructed only to |eta|<=2.5), so the unmeasured 2.0-2.5 region likely degrades efficiency, making 0.83 a defensible eta-averaged compromise. The proposed alternative ~0.87 matches the measured >0.85 plateau floor; both the keep-0.83 and revise-to-0.87 options are reasonable and properly hedged. The specific plot-read '~0.85-0.90' beyond the >0.85 floor is not independently verifiable, but the >0.85 floor and the eta-coverage mismatch are both solidly sourced.

per_coefficient.name: eff_endcap_highpt (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>100)
per_coefficient.note: Uncertainty wording loosely supported by Sec 6.1 ('<1% as ESC_T increases', stated for reco efficiency generally). But the precise plot-read '~0.90-0.97 (endcap high-ESC_T plateau)' cannot be confirmed cold: Fig.23b curve values are not in the extractable text, and the x-axis ends at 100 GeV so pt>100 is beyond the plotted range. per_coefficient.name: C_central (constant term, |eta|<=3.0)

(2)): 'The combined (ECAL+HCAL) calorimeter energy resolution was measured in a pion test beam [24] to be sigma/E = 110%/sqrt(E) (+) 9%, (2)'. per_coefficient.name: S_central (stochastic term, |eta|<=3.0)
per_coefficient.note: Same Eq. (2) in arXiv:1706.04965 Sec. 2.4: 'sigma/E = 110%/sqrt(E) (+) 9%'. MEASURED stochastic coefficient = 110% (1.10), exactly as extracted. (d) Numeric evals at eta=0 reproduce exactly: pT=30 ->1.099, pT=100 ->1.031, pT=1000 ->1.003. All cited locators are real and correct: the abstract text matches verbatim; Eq.(38) is in Sec.8 with the exact NSC form sqrt(sgn(N)N^2/pT^2 + S^2/pT + C^2) and Fig.36 reference; the headline uncertainties (below 3% pT>30 |eta|<5.0; below 1% barrel |eta|<1.3 excl. flavor; 0.32% at pT~165-330 GeV |eta|<0.8) are exact. per_coefficient.name: eff_lowpt_turnon
per_coefficient.note: Confirmed that the source quotes NO efficiency value below pT=20 GeV, so the card's hard pT>10 cut (eff=0 below) is a modeling convention the source cannot confirm or refute. Verbatim source: 'As a function of pT between 20 GeV and 200 GeV (where the efficiency is measured with reasonably small uncertainty), the loose ID efficiency is constant...' (Sec. 6). Table 3 caption: 'Efficiencies for several reconstruction+ID algorithms... for muons with pT > 20 GeV.' Figure 7 caption: '...for loose (left) and tight (right) muons with pT > 20 GeV.' The extraction's 'not-tabulated / cannot-determine' verdict and 'keep current' are correct. Note the 10-20 GeV plateau in the card is an extrapolation below the measured range, as the extraction states.

per_coefficient.name: eff_barrel_plateau
per_coefficient.note: Table 3 verbatim, MuonID rows, |eta| region 0.0<|eta|<0.9: Loose 99.75±0.02; Medium 98.25±0.02; Tight 96.00±0.03 (Data eff. [%]). All three extracted values and stat uncertainties match exactly. The ID systematic of ~1% is confirmed verbatim: 'The uncertainties are estimated to be at the level of 1% for ID and 0.5% for isolation.' The extraction's verdict 'card-pessimistic' is justified: card's 0.95 is below every cut-based working point in the barrel; it is ~1% below Tight ID (96.0%). The eta binning mismatch is real: card splits at |eta|=1.5 while source bins at |eta|=0.9 — correctly flagged.

per_coefficient.name: eff_endcap_plateau
per_coefficient.note: Table 3 verbatim, MuonID rows, |eta| region 0.9<|eta|<2.4: Loose 99.77±0.02; Medium 98.55±0.02; Tight 97.46±0.04 (Data eff. [%]). Matches extracted values exactly. Source text confirms: 'The tight ID efficiency varies between 95% and 99%, depending on eta, and the data and simulation agree to within 1-3%' (Sec. 6). Card's 0.95 is below all measured WPs in the endcap; 'card-pessimistic' is justified. The note that the card's 1.5-2.4 bin is a sub-range of the source's 0.9-2.4 bin is correct.

per_coefficient.name: eff_outside_acceptance
per_coefficient.note: Detector description (Sec. 2) verbatim: 'The muon system is located outside the solenoid and covers the range |eta| < 2.4.' Table 3 tabulates efficiencies only up to |eta|=2.4. Also Sec.4: '99% of the muons produced within the geometrical acceptance of the muon system are reconstructed.' The card's zero efficiency beyond |eta|=2.4 is the correct geometric statement. 'consistent' / 'keep current' is justified.

verifications.corrections: Values, locators, uncertainties, and verdicts are all accurate against the cited source (arXiv:1804.04528, Table 3 and Sec. 6, verified from the arXiv PDF text). One minor locator imprecision: the ~1% ID systematic is on the page-21 line 'The uncertainties are estimated to be at the level of 1% for ID and 0.5% for isolation' (just below Table 3), NOT the 'line 1051' the extraction cited for eff_endcap (line ~1051 in the PDF text concerns the muon-in-jet isolation mislabeling, ~5% barrel / ~15% endcap, an unrelated quantity). Also a small attribution nuance: Table 3's stated stat-from-fit uncertainties are described in the caption as applying to the scale factors; the Data eff. column uncertainties share the same fitting-stat origin, so labeling them 'statistical, from fit' is acceptable. No value corrections needed.

per_coefficient.name: eff_lowpt_central (|eta|<=1.5, 0.1<pt<=1.0)
per_coefficient.note: Extraction's 'no-source' verdict is correct. Read the cited paper (1804.04528) COLD: efficiency is measured only for pT>20 GeV. Sec 6.2, line 1080-1083: 'using a tracker track as the probe leads to a high combinatorial background in low-pT bins, which can result in large uncertainties in the background subtraction method.' Figs 7/8 and Table 3 are all captioned 'for muons with pT > 20 GeV.' No value at 0.1-1 GeV. The card value 0.75 has no counterpart in this source; CANNOT be confirmed/revised from it, exactly as the extraction states. Web search located no better clean tabulated public CMS value at 0.1-1 GeV. The 0.75 is an ad-hoc fast-sim turn-on value.

per_coefficient.name: eff_plateau_central (|eta|<=1.5, 1<pt<=1e3)
per_coefficient.note: Verbatim confirmed. Sec 6.2 line 1087-1090: 'The loose ID efﬁciency exceeds 99% over the entire η range, and the data and simulation agree to within 1%. As a function of pT between 20 GeV and 200 GeV (where the efﬁciency is measured with reasonably small uncertainty), the loose ID efﬁciency is constant with ﬂuctuations well within 1%.' Table 3 (lines 1296-1300): Loose ID, 0.0<|η|<0.9 = 99.75 ± 0.02. Sec 5 line 324-326: 'about 99% of the muons produced within the geometrical acceptance of the muon system are reconstructed either as a global muon track or as a tracker muon track.' Card 0.99 plateau matches measured >99% Loose ID; difference within ~1% systematic. 'keep current' is justified.

per_coefficient.name: eff_highpt_rolloff_central (|eta|<=1.5, pt>1e3)
per_coefficient.note: Extraction's 'no-source' verdict is correct. Sec 7 (line 1349-1353) is titled 'Momentum scale and resolution': 'For muons with pT > 200 GeV, combining information from the muon system with information from the inner tracker signiﬁcantly improves the momentum measurement.' This addresses momentum scale/resolution, NOT a reconstruction-efficiency decrease. No figure/table in the paper reports any reco-efficiency roll-off above 1 TeV (or at any high pT). The exp(0.5 - pt*5e-4) factor and its coefficients (0.5, 5.0e-4) are unsourced ad-hoc modeling, as stated.

per_coefficient.name: eff_lowpt_endcap (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, 0.1<pt<=1.0)
per_coefficient.note: Same as central low-pT bin: 'no-source' verdict is correct. The cited paper measures efficiency only for pT>20 GeV (Table 3, Figs 7/8 captions; low-pT large-background caveat at line 1080-1083). No endcap value tabulated at 0.1-1 GeV. Card 0.70 is an unsourced fast-sim turn-on value; cannot be confirmed/revised from this source. No better clean public value located.

per_coefficient.name: eff_plateau_endcap (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, 1<pt<=1e3)
per_coefficient.note: Verbatim confirmed. Table 3 (lines 1301-1302): Loose ID, 0.9<|η|<2.4 = 99.77 ± 0.02. Sec 6.2 line 1087: 'loose ID efﬁciency exceeds 99% over the entire η range.' Muon system acceptance is |η|<2.4 (line 70: 'The muon system... covers the range |η| < 2.4'; line 94 endcap defined 1.2<|η|<2.4). Card 0.98 endcap plateau is ~1.8% below the measured 99.77%, so the 'card-pessimistic' verdict is well-founded. The optional upward revision to ~0.99 is justified by Table 3; keeping 0.98 as conservative is also defensible. Note table value is reco+ID relative-to-tracker (Loose ID), not a pure standalone tracking efficiency, so treating it as an upper guide for the card plateau is reasonable.

per_coefficient.name: eff_highpt_rolloff_endcap (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>1e3)
per_coefficient.note: Same as central high-pT term: 'no-source' verdict is correct. Sec 7 ('Momentum scale and resolution') reports momentum-measurement improvement for pT>200 GeV (line 1352), not an efficiency roll-off. No endcap reco-efficiency decrease above 1 TeV is reported anywhere in the paper. The 0.98*exp(0.5 - pt*5e-4) factor and coefficients are unsourced modeling choices, as stated.

per_coefficient.name: eff_outside_acceptance (|eta|>2.5 and pt<=0.1)
per_coefficient.note: Confirmed. Muon-system geometric acceptance is |η|<2.4 (line 70: 'The muon system... covers the range |η| < 2.4'; Sec 5 line 324-326 references 'geometrical acceptance of the muon system'). Zero efficiency outside acceptance and below pT threshold is physically correct. The extraction's caveat is accurate and important: the true muon acceptance edge is |η|=2.4, but the card extends its non-zero plateau to |η|=2.5, so the card slightly overstates coverage in 2.4<|η|<=2.5. This eta-edge mismatch is correctly flagged.

verifications.corrections: No corrections to the extraction. Every value, locator, and uncertainty I checked against the cold-read source (PDF of arXiv:1804.04528, extracted via PyMuPDF) matched verbatim: Sec 5 ~99% reconstruction within |eta|<2.4 (lines 324-326, 70); Sec 6.2 'loose ID efficiency exceeds 99%... constant with fluctuations well within 1%' for pT 20-200 GeV (lines 1087-1090); Table 3 Loose ID = 99.75±0.02 (0.0<|eta|<0.9) and 99.77±0.02 (0.9<|eta|<2.4) (lines 1296-1303); efficiency measured only for pT>20 GeV; Sec 7 covers momentum scale/resolution, NOT efficiency roll-off (lines 1349-1353). The four 'no-source' verdicts (two low-pT turn-on bins, two high-pT exponential roll-off terms) are confirmed: these card values/coefficients are genuinely unsupported by this paper and no better clean public CMS value was located. Minor observations (not corrections to the extraction, which already flags both): (a) Table 3 Loose-ID figures are reco+ID efficiencies relative to tracker tracks, slightly broader than a pure 'tracking' efficiency, so using them to validate the card's tracking-efficiency plateau is approximate but appropriate; (b) the card's 2.5 vs the source's 2.4 acceptance edge is correctly noted in eta_binning_mismatch and the outside-acceptance coefficient. Overall confidence 'medium' is appropriately calibrated given that 4 of 7 coefficients have no source.

per_coefficient.name: eff_lowpt_allEta (pt<=10 GeV)
per_coefficient.note: Source 1502.02702 IS real and the phrase 'the threshold is chosen to be 10 GeV' exists (p.21, my extracted line 1492), BUT the cited locator 'Sec. 6' is WRONG: that sentence is in Section 5 (conversion track reconstruction) and refers to the CONVERTED-PHOTON track-pair pT threshold ('The threshold on the converted photon pT as measured by the tracks ... the threshold is chosen to be 10 GeV'), not a photon-ID/selection threshold. The extraction's rationale also claims '25<pT<200 GeV' ID benchmark; this is unsupported — 2012.06888 states the photon ID efficiency is measured 'above 20 GeV for photons' (my line 3503), and 1502.02702 Fig 18/tag-and-probe uses pT>15 GeV / 20-30 GeV. The 0.00 floor below 10 GeV is a defensible Delphes modeling convention (no source tabulates efficiency below threshold), so the 'keep current' outcome is fine, but the specific locator and benchmark numbers cited are not confirmed.

per_coefficient.name: eff_barrel (|eta|<=1.5, pt>10)
per_coefficient.note: The anchor is CONFIRMED verbatim: 2012.06888 Sec 7.2.1 (my lines 3203/3225): 'The "loose" working point has an average signal efficiency of about 90%'. Fig 27 is CONFIRMED: 'Photon identification efficiency ... for the loose cut-based (left) ... as functions of the photon ET', shown in FOUR eta ranges (0.00-0.80, 0.80-1.44, 1.57-2.00, 2.00-2.50), and 'ratios are within 5% from unity for all the cut-based identification working points' (my line 3520). HOWEVER the extracted 'barrel plateau ~0.88-0.93 at high ET' cannot be verified — figure marker values are not present in extractable text, and the source gives only a single ~90% average, not a barrel-specific plateau number. The proposed revision 0.92+/-0.05 is a reasonable interpolation off the ~90% average, but is NOT a source-tabulated value; calling 0.95 'mildly optimistic' vs a 90% average is a defensible judgement but rests on equating Delphes reco+ID with the loose-ID average.

per_coefficient.name: eff_endcap (1.5<|eta|<=2.5, pt>10)
per_coefficient.note: The qualitative basis is CONFIRMED: 2012.06888 (my lines 3520-3522) states data/MC 'ratios are within 5% from unity' and explicitly notes 'the variation of ECAL noise with time, which affects the sigma_ieta_ieta variable in low- and medium-ET electrons and photons in the endcap' — matching the extraction's ECAL-noise endcap note. The barrel>endcap ordering is consistent with the four-range Fig 27. BUT the specific endcap plateau '0.85-0.90' is NOT tabulated; the only number is the global ~90% loose-WP average. So 0.85 being 'within the endcap loose-WP plateau range' cannot be confirmed from text — it is a plausible reading of unreadable figure markers. 'keep current' is defensible but unverified at the quoted precision.

per_coefficient.name: eff_forward (|eta|>2.5)
per_coefficient.note: 2012.06888 Sec 7.2.3 (my line 3254): 'Photon candidates with ET > 15 GeV, |eta| < 2.5, and satisfying very loose preselection requirements are used'. Fig 27 eta ranges terminate at 2.50. Photon ID efficiency is defined/measured only for |eta|<2.5, so the card's 0.00 beyond 2.5 correctly encodes the acceptance edge. NOTE: the ECAL itself physically extends to |eta|<3.0 (barrel |eta|<1.48, endcap 1.48<|eta|<3.00, my line ~310), so the cut at 2.5 is a tracker/electron-veto/ID-measurement acceptance limit rather than a hard ECAL edge — the extraction's phrasing 'beyond ECAL acceptance' is slightly imprecise but the 0.00 value and |eta|<2.5 photon-candidate requirement are correct.

The verbatim anchors (loose/medium/tight ~90%/80%/70%, Sec 7.2.1; data/MC within 5%, line 3520; ECAL-noise endcap sigma_ieta_ieta note; |eta|<2.5 photon-candidate requirement; 1502.02702 Table 3 and Fig 18 for pT>15 GeV incl. electron veto) are all CONFIRMED and correctly cited.
